WDIO is a hugely popular E2E testing framework for Web Applications. This also includes hybrid apps. It can drive a real browser and simulate a user interacting with the app. WDIO can work with apps that use any web framework but there are certain advantages if the testing framework integrates with the web framework. If this is the case, the tests could be much simpler to write and mainly, much more reliable. Reliability is of paramount importance for E2E tests that typically struggle with flakiness so any improvement can have significant effect on the TCO of testing process

documents.t: By following the above instructions, you will ensure that dialogs opened using the KloController.openDialog API are closed consistently and correctly with the KloController.closeDialog API. This approach helps avoid potential issues and improves the stability and maintainability of the application.
Screenshot
Screenshot

Dialogs opened via the KloController.openDialog API should be closed using the KloController.closeDialog API, not the sap.m.Dialog's close method. The sap.m.Dialog's close method should only be used when the dialog was opened via the sap.m.Dialog.open() method.

It has been noted that some applications are using the sap.m.Dialog's close method to close dialogs that were opened via the KloController.openDialog API. This can result in inconsistencies and potential issues. To maintain uniformity and prevent problems, it is essential that the KloController.closeDialog API is used to close dialogs opened by the KloController.openDialog API.

The page refers to the single visible screen of the application. The page is the topmost layer of an application. It will be embedded with a pageLayout.

By default, when a simple select query is fired on any entity, it returns all data that is present in the entity. But, by enabling and configuring row wise authorization on an entity, the list of records accessible to any user can be controlled using access tokens.

Module: EndpointBean

new EndPointBean(rootEntity, endpointID, epType, s_channel, onlydirtyobject, onlyRootEntity?): EndPointBean Parameters​ Name Type Attributes Description rootEntity KloEntity @@@ endpointID any @@@ epType EndpointType @@@ s_channel ChannelType @@@ onlydirtyobject boolean @@@ onlyRootEntity boolean Optional @@@ Returns​ EndPointBean

Name Type Default Description channel ChannelType filter on qualified endpoint to narrow down the receivers. dependentEntity @@@ addition entities alnog with BO endPointID string this can be single ID as per specified type or array of IDS ass per specified types. endPointType EndpointType endPointType and endPointID togather determines set of endpoint to send the message entityObject KloEntity BO to send as message onlyRootEntity boolean if true only the root object will be in message else its child also will be in Message onlydirtyobject boolean if true builds only dirty object in message else loads the complete entity object

addDependantEntities(entity): KloEntity[] Parameters​ Name Type Description entity KloEntity The KloEntity instance to add as a dependent entity Returns​ KloEntity[] - Array of all dependent entities including the newly added one Description​ Adds a dependent entity to be included in the data message sent to endpoints. Dependent entities are additional entities that should be sent along with the main entity object. This is useful when you need to send related data that may not be directly linked but is contextually important. Example​ let endpointBean = eventContext.addEndpoint("USER001", EndpointType.USER, ChannelType.DEVICE, orderEntity); let customerEntity = await txn.loadEntityP("d_customer", customerKey); endpointBean.addDependantEntities(customerEntity); // Customer info sent along with order See​ getDependantEntities to retrieve the list of dependent entities

getDependantEntities(): KloEntity[] Returns​ KloEntity[] - Array of KloEntity instances that are configured as dependent entities Description​ Gets the list of dependent entities that have been added to this endpoint bean. Dependent entities are additional entities that will be included in the data message along with the primary entity object when the message is sent to endpoints. Example​ let endpointBean = eventContext.addEndpoint("USER001", EndpointType.USER, ChannelType.DEVICE, orderEntity); endpointBean.addDependantEntities(customerEntity); endpointBean.addDependantEntities(productEntity); let dependents = endpointBean.getDependantEntities(); console.log("Number of dependent entities:", dependents.length); See​ addDependantEntities to add dependent entities

documents.t: A .certSigningRequest file is a critical part of the certificate generation process in iOS development. It is used to create a code-signing certificate, which is necessary for signing your iOS apps for distribution via In-House or Ad Hoc methods. The CSR file contains information about the developer or the organization, including the public key, which is used by Apple to generate the appropriate signing certificate.If you want to create a new Certificate, then follow the steps below. Open the keychain Access as shown in the below screenshot. Click on Request a Certificate From a Certificate Authority as shown in the below screenshot. Click on Keychain Access as shown in the below screenshot. Fill the below details as shown in the below screenshot. The user's email address plays an indirect role in the code-signing process since it is linked to your Apple Developer account and included in the signing certificate's metadata. While the Keychain holds the signing certificate and private key, it does not store the email address in plain text. Instead, the email is embedded within the certificate's metadata, which identifies the developer or organization. In short: Email is used to identify the developer in the signing certificate. Keychain stores the certificate and private key needed for signing the app, enabling secure app distribution and code signing. The CA Email Address is a part of the Issuer information within a certificate and provides a way to contact the Certificate Authority that issued the certificate. It serves as a point of contact for issues related to the certificate, such as validation, renewal, or revocation. You can find the CA's email address in the certificate metadata, which can be inspected in various tools like Keychain Access on macOS or by viewing the certificate details in a web browser. Save the certificate as shown in the below screenshot. Now you can see the certificate as shown in the below screenshot.

documents.t: Certificates ensure your app is properly authorized for development, testing, and distribution. They act as a security mechanism to ensure that only authorized developers and apps can interact with Apple devices. Without these certificates, your app cannot be installed on devices or distributed via the App Store. If you want to create a new Certificate, then follow the steps below. Open your Apple developer account. Click on Certificates as shown in the below screenshot Click on the create ( + ) button as shown below. Select the In-House and Ad Hoc check box and click on continue. In-House: Choose this if you need to distribute apps internally within a company, especially if the app is for internal use and will be installed on many devices within your organization. This is the best choice for enterprise-level apps and internal tools. Ad Hoc: Choose Ad Hoc distribution if you have a small group of testers or specific clients who need to test or review your app before release. This is the best choice for beta testing or distributing an app to a limited number of users. Both methods are critical for scenarios where an app is not intended for public release via the App Store but needs to be tested or used by a controlled group. Enabling Services: Used to enable services like Push Notifications, iCloud, In-App Purchases, Game Center, and more. Managing Versions: Helps to manage different versions of the app, such as production and staging. App Group and Keychain Sharing: Facilitates data sharing between multiple apps. App Distribution: Ensures correct signing and submission for App Store or TestFlight. App Extensions: Ties extensions (e.g., widgets, share extensions) to the main app. Security: Ensures app integrity during installation and distribution. documents.t: Identifiers play a central role in iOS app development, as they are used to uniquely identify different components and services across the Apple ecosystem. They are essential for ensuring proper code signing, testing, distribution, and enabling services like Push Notifications, In-App Purchases, and iCloud.If you want to create new Identifiers, then follow the steps below. Click on ( + ) button as shown in the below screenshot. In the Apple Developer Portal, App IDs are essential for associating your iOS app with Apple's developer services. By creating either Explicit App IDs or Wildcard App IDs, you ensure that your app is properly configured for code signing, provisioning profiles, and services such as Push Notifications and In-App Purchases. It's critical to select the right type of App ID based on your app’s needs and how you intend to distribute it (via App Store, Ad Hoc, or In-House). Select App IDs as shown in the below screenshot. Provide the details and scroll down The Description field in the Identifiers & Profiles section of the Apple Developer Portal is a valuable tool for organizing, managing, and tracking your app development and distribution assets. It improves clarity and helps developers and teams keep track of multiple configurations, ensuring smooth app development and distribution workflows. The Bundle ID is a critical part of the iOS development and distribution process. It uniquely identifies your app, associates it with your developer account, and enables it to interact with various Apple services. Properly setting and managing your Bundle ID is essential for a smooth app development workflow, particularly when managing app versions, provisioning profiles, and services like push notifications and in-app purchase Click on the Push Notification check box and click on continue. Push notifications are an incredibly powerful tool for engaging users, delivering timely information, and enhancing user retention. By leveraging Apple Push Notification Service (APNs), iOS developers can integrate push notifications into their apps to send personalized, real-time updates to users. However, it's important to use push notifications thoughtfully, respecting user preferences and ensuring the content is relevant and non-intrusive. Below are the list of new features/bug fixes developed as a part of the release in this module. Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-15475 UI Editor: On rename of any page element, select the existing text(so that user can start typing new value directly) Tools:UI Editor No UI Editor: When renaming a page element, the existing text is selected, enabling the user to start typing the new value right away. After the rename dialog box is opened the text inside the input box is automatically selected. PROC-9723 Message Monitor - Endpoint information on popover Tools: Message monitor No On hovering over the endpoint, the details will be displayed in a popover. End point Details like Registration date, last active date ,Last transaction, device type and status will be shown. The popover functionality has been added to show the endpoint details when hovered over. PROC-15240 BOL Editor -Add validation to restrict changing the primary keys in the child flavor Tools: Bol Editor No The primary key cannot be modified in entities passed from the parent app to the child app, nor in entities created using an older flavor version. These restrictions are in place to maintain data integrity and consistency across different versions and flavors. PROC-16164 Validation while adding and saving in App Hierarchy Detail Section Tools -System Admin No App Hierarchy Detail Section added Validation. A validation is now in place to prevent creating cyclic JSON structures when assigning a parent to a flavor, ensuring no crashes occur. Additionally, if a flavor version is deleted and a new version of the same flavor is assigned immediately, it won't work. The user must save changes before adding the new version. Details: App Hierarchy

Issue No. Description Adoption / Script PROC-24144 Unnecessary Permission Requests in APK for KloRemark and Document Upload Removed spurious permission prompts in the Android APK: KloRemark no longer requests microphone permission on screen load without user interaction, and Document Upload no longer triggers unnecessary storage permissions. Issue No. Description Adoption / Script PROC-26524 Enhancement: Enforce Default Permissions and Validation for New Roles At DEV Systems, after a new role creation, a warning box will be shown on the screen, to inform the developers about maintaining the permissions for that new role, to avoid Access Denied scenario for the respective users belonging to that role. Issue No. Description Adoption / Script PROC-26816 Business AI: Application Workflow Context Implementation — POC and Phase 1 Completed POC and Phase 1 implementation of application workflow context for Business AI. The AI assistant can now understand and reason about the workflow state of the current application, enabling context-aware suggestions. N/A PROC-26745 Business AI: VH Query Suggestion Display to User Business AI now surfaces Value Help query suggestions to the user during data entry. Below are the list of new features/bug fixes developed as a part of the release in this module. Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-27362 OData BO Support – Deep Update (Header + Child updates in a single call) No BOL Extended OData support to allow deep update operations where both header and child entity data can be updated in a single API call. Previously, multi-level updates required sequential requests, increasing round trips. Clients can send nested JSON payloads containing parent entity properties along with child entity arrays. Child entities are automatically matched by parent key - existing children are updated, and new children are created.All operations are committed in a single transaction with full validation support. This significantly reduces overhead for complex entity hierarchies. Document Link Status: Tested PROC-27343 BOL Node 512 MB Stability Verification & Issue Resolution No BOL Verified stability of the BOL Node running under a 512 MB memory constraint and resolved all identified issues. Ensures the platform operates reliably within constrained memory environments for applicable deployments. Status: Done - Closed PROC-27366 Middleware: 1000 messages with no_sequence=0 took 17 minutes to process No BOL - Middleware Resolved a middleware throughput issue where 1000 messages with no_sequence=0 took 17 minutes to complete against only 1 minute of actual processing time (16 minutes idle). Queuing and dispatch logic has been optimized to eliminate idle wait between message batches. Status: Tested PROC-26465 Middleware: Default retry delay for deadlock/lock wait should be increased No BOL - Middleware For the middleware retry settings for Inbound Messages, the RetryDelaySeconds default value has been changed to 1 second in the config.json file. If it’s already overridden, then that value is not changed. Document Link Status: Tested PROC-25080 Transport log showing source and target landscape as "undefined" No BOL - Transport Fixed a transport logging defect where source and target landscape names appeared as "undefined" in the transport log. Landscape identifiers are now correctly resolved and displayed in all transport log entries. Status: Tested PROC-26541 Indexing required on Users Permissions table – madm_user_permissions No BOL Added a composite index on the r_user_id & r_landscape column in the madm_user_permissions table to improve query performance for user-based permission lookups. Status: Tested PROC-26503 Remove deprecated entity reference button or handle logic in BOL / BOL Editor No BOL / BOL Editor Removed the deprecated entity reference-based condition button from the BOL Editor UI. Updated the underlying logic to prevent duplicate condition generation and to ignore deprecated backward-compatibility paths, eliminating developer confusion caused by legacy UI artifacts. Status: Tested PROC-26994 Custom template should be enabled for OTP Services No BOL OTP notification services can now use custom message templates. Previously OTP messages were fixed to a system template. Developers can now configure custom templates for OTP emails and SMS channels, enabling branded OTP communications per application. Status: Tested Reference Document : Notification Developer Guide PROC-26106 Attachment: setAttachmentP() not working on server side No BOL Fixed a bug where setAttachmentP() called from server-side logic (entity callbacks or controllers) threw a "File Write Failed" error. The server-side attachment API now correctly processes and persists file data. Status: Tested PROC-25752 Phase 02 Runtime – PIVOT/REPORT/CHART: Server-side pivoting No BOL Implemented Phase 2 of server-side data pivoting. Pivot, Report, and Chart data transformations are now computed on the server instead of the client browser, reducing client-side load and significantly improving performance for large datasets. Status: Tested User Guide link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1oNQqNsgTLLFqtPn7914ggasXzJTDXc-oSo6QBYq9T6Y/edit?tab=t.0 PROC-22355 API Versioning Behavior Creates Misleading User Experience No BOL Corrected API URL versioning behaviour that was ignoring explicitly requested patch versions and automatically redirecting to the latest patch. API version resolution now honours the requested version, giving developers predictable and accurate versioning. Status: Done - Closed PROC-25409 BOL Editor: Excel-uploaded entry not present after refreshing (Rollup status and Status Config) No BOL Editor Fixed a persistence bug in BOL Editor where entries added via Excel upload were not retained after a page refresh in the Rollup Status and Status Config views. Uploaded entries now correctly persist to the database and reload on refresh. Status: Tested PROC-24593 BOL Node 512 MB – OData GET Services No BOL Validated and ensured OData GET service functionality is fully operational in the BOL Node 512 MB memory configuration. Addressed compatibility issues specific to this constrained memory deployment scenario. Status: Tested PROC-25001 BOL/Metadata: adding vh to query parameter not updating query generation No BOL Fixed a metadata query generation bug where adding a value help (vh) to a query parameter did not correctly update the generated query. The query generator now correctly incorporates vh-based parameters, ensuring accurate data retrieval. Status: Tested PROC-24749 Training: get$Role() returning empty object {} in controller and console No BOL Resolved an issue where get$Role() returned {} instead of the user's role data when called from a controller. The function now correctly retrieves and returns the active user role, consistent with $SYSTEM.roleId behaviour. Status: Tested PROC-27146 Safeguards to prevent recursive invocation between entity callback and CommitP API No BOL Added runtime safeguards to detect and break recursive call loops that occur when an entity callback triggers a CommitP API call, which in turn re-invokes the entity callback. Prevents infinite recursion and stack overflow in server-side business logic. Validation added in case the same transaction is being used for commitP() from callbacks throwing error as “Transaction commit is already in progress. Please wait for the current commit to finish before calling commit again.“. e.g., Developers should not use commitP() by using the same transaction at the rules callbacks - get the transaction from oEvent (function parameter) and use that for commitP() later on in the rules callback. Document Link 1, Document Link 2 Status: Tested PROC-26611 SEAM4: error_code missing in kloerror when commitP fails No BOL Fixed a bug where the error_code field was absent in the kloerror response object when a commitP operation failed. The error_code is now correctly populated, enabling downstream error handling to distinguish and respond to specific failure types. Status: Tested

Previously this selection was only available via Developer AI. Also includes fixes for known issues in the wizard screen creation flow. Developers can now create wizard-type screens entirely from the UI Editor. Status: Tested PROC-26662 REL_26/15-18 HomePage Editor: KL0018 testcase failing, Navigation not working No KloTouch Fixed a navigation regression in the HomePage Editor where the KL0018 test case was failing due to broken navigation on the homepage screen. Navigation flows on homepage-type screens now behave correctly per the defined test specification. Status: Tested PROC-25246 Need busyIndicator while vh is loading data for F4 No KloTouch Added a busy indicator that displays while value help (vh) data is being fetched for F4 field searches. Previously the F4 popup gave no visual feedback during data load, creating confusion about system responsiveness. Status: Tested

Below are the list of new features/improvements developed as a part of the release in this module. Feature Adoption Tool & Short Description PROC-27164 Business AI – Application Context implementation Phase 2 No Business AI Completed Phase 2 of the Application Context feature for Business AI. This phase integrates kloQuery callbacks and additional AI context scenarios, enabling Business AI to generate queries and responses with richer, application-aware data. Status: Tested Reference Guide - Business_AI_User_Guide PROC-26607 Developer AI – User/App level token limits and usage metrics No Developer AI Implemented configurable token limit enforcement and usage tracking at user and application level for Developer AI. Administrators can now set per-user and per-app token quotas; usage metrics are tracked for governance and cost control. Status: Tested PROC-27240 Developer AI – All LLM calls properly logged in LangSmith No Developer AI All LLM calls from Developer AI are now captured in LangSmith with proper, searchable names. Previously generic entries made it impossible to isolate individual AI call chains. Each call now appears with a meaningful identifier. Status: Tested PROC-27215 Developer AI – Early return on dependency failure in agents No Developer AI Added early-exit logic across RuleAgent, SchedulerAgent, NotificationAgent, and SampleDataAgent. If any upstream dependency fails mid-execution, the agent immediately returns a clear error instead of continuing with partial or misleading output. Status: Tested PROC-26921 Developer AI – Code files fetched from actual repository No Developer AI Developer AI now fetches existing code files directly from the version-controlled source repository instead of the local file system, ensuring AI modifications are based on the live codebase rather than potentially stale copies. Status: Tested PROC-27598 Developer AI – Qdrant not supporting 3072 dimensions No Developer AI Fixed a vector storage compatibility issue where Qdrant rejected 3072-dimension embeddings. The Qdrant collection is now correctly configured to support the required dimensionality for the AI embedding model in use. Status: Tested PROC-27565 Developer AI – Incorrect accountId in payload causing metadata save error No Developer AI Corrected a payload bug where an incorrect accountId caused AI metadata save operations to fail. The payload now correctly resolves and includes the authenticated user's accountId before submission. Status: Tested PROC-27214 Developer AI – Run-only-jobs includes screen creation in response No Developer AI Fixed a response scoping issue where selecting "run only jobs" in Developer AI still returned screen creation results. The agent now correctly restricts execution and response to the selected job types only. Status: Tested PROC-27128 Developer AI – Errors in Google Cloud logs during normal operation No Developer AI Resolved error-level log entries in Google Cloud logs triggered by normal Developer AI operations. Log levels have been corrected and error handling improved to eliminate false-alarm log noise. Status: Tested PROC-27034 Developer AI – Handle transient fields in SampleDataAgent/RuleAgents/NotificationAgent No Developer AI Updated agents to correctly differentiate Regular, Transient, and Calculated property types. Previously transient fields were incorrectly included in insert operations, causing errors and invalid data generation. Status: Tested PROC-27024 Developer AI – getEntitiesDetails API returning all properties as Regular No Developer AI Fixed a logic bug where getEntitiesDetails returned all properties as "Regular" regardless of actual type. Property types are now correctly derived from entity configuration (Transient, Calculated, Regular). Status: Tested PROC-27021 Developer AI – Attachment and GeoLocation must be transient, not regular No Developer AI Corrected property type classification for Attachment and GeoLocation to Transient, as these are not persisted directly in the entity table. Ensures correct handling by all AI agents. Status: Tested PROC-26309 Developer AI – Clear message when requested App is not found No Developer AI Improved error handling so Developer AI returns a clear, actionable message when a requested application does not exist, instead of a generic failure. Status: Tested PROC-26281 Developer AI – Handle concurrent multi-user requests No Developer AI Implemented concurrency handling for simultaneous multi-user Developer AI requests. Each user's workflow now executes in full isolation, preventing session cross-contamination. Status: Tested PROC-26278 Developer AI – Use incremental IDs for screens, remove datekey No Developer AI Replaced timestamp-based datekeys in AI-generated screen IDs with deterministic incremental IDs. Added duplicate ID checks. Produces cleaner, predictable identifiers for AI-generated screens. Status: Tested PROC-26277 Developer AI – Multiple subscreen layouts incorrectly added to one subscreen No Developer AI Fixed a screen generation defect where multiple subscreen layout definitions were attached to the same subscreen. Each subscreen now receives only its designated layout. Status: Tested PROC-26271 Developer AI – Validate each metadata item created for screen No Developer AI Added per-metadata validation during AI screen generation. Each generated metadata item is individually validated before persistence, allowing errors to be caught granularly. Status: Tested PROC-25033 React Phase 01 – Playwright automation No React UI Implemented Playwright-based automated test coverage for React Phase 01 deliverables. Establishes a regression test baseline for the React UI track. Status: Tested

Developer Level 2 — Advanced Track Enhancing the Customer Complaints Application This track does not build a new application. Every session goes back into the SAME Customer Complaints app built in Developer Level 1, and layers a new advanced capability onto it — the same end-to-end build approach used in the Level 1 guide. Prerequisite: Developer Level 1 completion is mandatory. Proposed dates are placeholders (one session per working day, starting Mon 07 Sep 2026) — confirm actual start date and cadence.

Developer Level 1 was built as an end-to-end project: one real application — the Customer Complaints Application — built up session by session. This Level 2 guide follows the same approach: no new application is created. Every session below re-opens the entities, pages, entity files, and controllers already built in Level 1 and extends them with an advanced capability, so trainees see how real applications evolve rather than practicing features in isolation. Topics are drawn from the Training Topics sheet, filtered to entries tagged “Developer Level 2,” and mapped onto concrete enhancements of the existing app. Tool names use the current naming glossary, with legacy names noted where relevant.

Sessions must be taken in order — each session's steps assume the previous session's enhancement is already in place, exactly as in the Level 1 guide. Session Date Topic Area Application Enhancement Session 1 Mon, 07 Sep 2026 Advanced BOL & Data Modelling Network Modes — Offline-Ready Properties · Sort Order & Entity Index · Entity Rules — Auto-Escalation on Update · Query Rules — Role-Based Field Masking · BOL Transaction — Close Complaint with Feedback Session 2 Tue, 08 Sep 2026 Advanced Page Builder & Client-Side Debugging Embedded Section — Complaint Timeline · Advanced kloControls · TransNode onArrive & navigateId · Server-Side Debugging & Auto Update Data Session 3 Wed, 09 Sep 2026 Security, Permissions & Data Access Design-Time Permissions · Row Wise Auth · Data Access Rules & User Access Summary · Role Permissions (Runtime) & Permission Logs Session 4 Thu, 10 Sep 2026 Offline, Middleware & Bulk Data Local Archive · Initial Downloads · Middleware — Device & SAP · KloSectionXlsx — Bulk Customer Import Session 5 Fri, 11 Sep 2026 Workflows, Scheduling & Notifications Escalation Approval Workflow · Scheduler — Nightly SLA Sweep · Notifications · deeplink & Banner Session 6 Mon, 14 Sep 2026 Reporting — Charts & Pivot Modeller kloChart — Status Breakdown · Advanced Chart — TAT Trend · Pivot Modeller Session 7 Tue, 15 Sep 2026 Monitoring & Troubleshooting Scheduler & Log Monitoring · Notification & Queue Monitoring · APK/IPA & Query Console Session 8 Wed, 16 Sep 2026 App Management, Branding & Deployment App Inheritance & Modification · Customer Branding · Git Repo & Active Sessions · App Migration to QA

Configure Network Modes so offline-relevant properties sync correctly to field devices. Apply Sort Order and an Entity Index to d_complaints for performance and predictable ordering. Extend the existing Entity Rules with a new auto-escalation rule. Extend the existing Query Rules with role-based field masking. Build a BOL Transaction that commits two entities atomically. What This Session Builds On Developer Level 1 (Sessions 1–5) built d_complaints with its properties, one Entity Rule (onCreateComplaint) and one Query Rule (beforeQ) on q_complaints. This session does not start a new entity — it goes back into the same d_complaints and q_complaints files and adds the advanced BOL capabilities on top.

A field IT Team member on a tablet needs complaint status and priority visible even with no signal, while internal notes stay server-side only. Meanwhile complaints are quietly sailing past SLA with no auto-flag, and a support rep spots that anyone on the IT Team can see a customer's full contact details in the list — details they never needed for their job.

Not every property should sync to a field device the same way. Configure Network Mode per property on d_complaints. # Action Detail 1 Open properties Procify Data Studio → d_complaints → Properties tab. 2 Restrict remark Set Network Mode = Online Only on remark — internal notes should not be cached on IT Team field devices. 3 Always sync core fields Set Network Mode = Always on complaint_id, s_status, priority so they remain visible even when the device is offline. 4 Save & update schema Save, then Update Schema, and confirm no errors.
documents.s: Part A — Network Modes — Offline-Ready Properties

documents.t: The complaints list currently has no defined default order and no index for the fields it is filtered on most. # Action Detail 1 Set Sort Order On priority: custom order CRITICAL > HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW. On created_on: DESCENDING as the secondary sort. 2 Create Entity Index Entity Index tab → Add → ID: idx_complaint_status_priority — fields: s_status, priority. 3 Update Schema Update Schema and verify the index is listed under the entity's Test → Data Browser diagnostics.
documents.s: Part B — Sort Order & Entity Index

documents.t: Reopen the same d_complaints.ts file from Level 1 Session 5 and add a second rule alongside onCreateComplaint. # Action Detail 1 Register the rule Rule tab → Add → Event Type: On Update | Channel: Always on Server | Clazz: this | Invocation Method: checkEscalation. 2 Implement checkEscalation If s_status is OPEN or INPROCESS and (today − created_on) > 3 days, set is_escalated = true. 3 Test Backdate a test record's created_on in Data Browser to 4 days ago, save, and confirm is_escalated flips to true.
documents.s: Part C — Entity Rules — Auto-Escalation on Update

documents.t: Extend q_complaints.ts — the same file where beforeQ was written in Level 1 Session 4 — with an afterQ rule. # Action Detail 1 Add afterQ Event Type: After Query. In the handler, if the requesting role is IT_TEAM, replace customer contact fields in each result row with ‘•••’. 2 Test as IT Team Log in as it_<prid> — confirm customer contact fields are masked in the list. 3 Test as Manager Log in as mgr_<prid> — confirm the same fields show full data.
documents.s: Part D — Query Rules — Role-Based Field Masking

documents.t: Combine a status update and a new voice record into one atomic operation. # Action Detail 1 Create the transaction Data Studio → new BOL Transaction Tx_CloseWithFeedback, covering d_complaints (update s_status = CLOSED) and d_complaint_voices (create feedback record). 2 Wire the button Add a ‘Close with Feedback’ action on s_detail_header that commits both TransNodes through this transaction. 3 Test atomicity Force the voice record to fail validation (e.g. leave it blank) and confirm the status change also rolls back — not just the voice record. Session 1 Checkpoint ✔ Network Modes verified in an offline emulation for at least 3 properties. ✔ s_complaints defaults to priority order; idx_complaint_status_priority exists and is used. ✔ checkEscalation rule fires correctly on a backdated test record. ✔ afterQ masks customer fields for IT_TEAM but not for Manager. ✔ Tx_CloseWithFeedback commits both entities together or rolls back together. Enhancement delivered: Extends the existing d_complaints / q_complaints files from Level 1 (not a new entity) with offline sync control, performance indexing, automatic SLA escalation, field-level data masking by role, and an atomic close-with-feedback commit.
documents.s: Part E — BOL Transaction — Close Complaint with Feedback

documents.t: Build a reusable Embedded Section and use it on two different pages. Add Advanced kloControls (rating, file uploader) to the detail screen. Configure TransNode onArrive and navigateId behaviour. Debug the Session 1 server-side rule using Server-Side Debugging. Enable Auto Update Data so the Manager's list refreshes without manual action. What This Session Builds On p_complaints was built manually in Level 1 Session 2 and styled in Session 6; p_complaint_dashboard was built in Session 5. Both existing pages are extended here — no new page is created from scratch.

A Manager opens a complaint and has to hunt across screens to see whether this customer has complained before. A rep marks a complaint resolved but there's no way to capture how satisfied the customer actually was, or attach a photo of a damaged product without emailing it separately.

Build one timeline section and reuse it in two places. # Action Detail 1 Create the section New section s_complaint_timeline (screenType: timeline) bound to a TransNode combining voices and status-change history. 2 Embed in detail In pa_comp_details, add a new section, mark it Embedded, and point its source to s_complaint_timeline. 3 Reuse on dashboard Add the same embedded section to p_complaint_dashboard as a ‘Recent Activity’ panel — confirming true cross-page reuse.
documents.s: Part A — Embedded Section — Complaint Timeline

documents.t: Add two controls that were not covered in Level 1's basic control set. # Action Detail 1 Add kloRating On s_detail_header, add a kloRating control bound to a new transient property t_satisfaction_score, visible only when s_status = CLOSED. 2 Add kloFileUploader On the attachments section, add kloFileUploader bound to the d_complaints_attachment relation built in Level 1. 3 Full Preview Confirm the rating control only appears on closed complaints and the uploader stores a file record correctly.

Make the detail screen smarter about what loads automatically and where links resolve to. # Action Detail 1 Configure onArrive On the detail TransNode, set onArrive to auto-load the 5 most recent related voices — no extra click required. 2 Configure navigateId On the ticket_id link control, set navigateId so it always resolves to pa_complaint_details, whether clicked from p_complaints or the dashboard's embedded timeline. 3 Test both entry points Click a complaint from the main list, then from the dashboard timeline — confirm both land on the same detail area correctly populated.

Debug the rule written in Session 1 and make the Manager's grid self-refreshing. # Action Detail 1 Attach debugger Set a breakpoint inside checkEscalation in VS Code and attach to the running Private Node. 2 Step through Trigger a save on a test complaint and step through the rule execution line by line. 3 Enable auto refresh On s_complaints, set Auto Update Data = true with a 30-second interval. 4 Verify Create a complaint as Employee in one browser tab; confirm it appears in the Manager's grid within 30 seconds without a manual refresh. Session 2 Checkpoint ✔ s_complaint_timeline renders correctly on both p_complaints and p_complaint_dashboard. ✔ kloRating and kloFileUploader function as specified. ✔ onArrive auto-loads voices; navigateId resolves correctly from both entry points. ✔ Breakpoint debugging confirmed inside checkEscalation. ✔ Manager's grid auto-refreshes within 30 seconds of a new complaint being created. Enhancement delivered: Adds a reusable complaint-history timeline, a satisfaction rating and attachment capture on resolution, smarter auto-loading/navigation, and a self-refreshing Manager grid — all on the existing pages built in Level 1.
documents.s: Part D — Server-Side Debugging & Auto Update Data

documents.t: Enforce CRUD restrictions server-side using design-time Permissions. Restrict IT Team visibility to their own team's complaints using Row Wise Auth. Scope customer data by region using Data Access Rules. Audit a user's effective access using User Access Summary. Grant, use, and revoke a temporary elevated Role Permission, and confirm it in Permission Logs. What This Session Builds On Level 1 Session 7 hid or disabled buttons per role using Vienable — a UI-level control only. This session enforces the same rules at the platform/security level so they hold even if a user calls the API directly.

An IT Team member who left last month still has delete rights if they call the API directly, even though the button is hidden in the UI. A regional manager can see every customer's complaints nationwide instead of just their region, and after an override was granted during an incident, nobody can say who approved it or when it was revoked.

Configure real CRUD restrictions, not just hidden buttons. # Action Detail 1 Configure Employee Employee role: Create + Read only. 2 Configure Manager Manager role: Create + Read + Update + Delete. 3 Configure IT Team IT Team role: Read + Update only. 4 Test server-side block Log in as emp_<prid> and confirm Delete is blocked even if attempted outside the hidden button (e.g. via a direct API call).

Restrict IT Team to only the complaints assigned to their own team. # Action Detail 1 Configure the rule Row Wise Auth on d_complaints: IT_TEAM role only receives rows where responsible_team = current user's team. 2 Test Log in as it_<prid> — confirm only assigned complaints appear, even via direct navigation to a different complaint's URL.

Scope customer master data regionally and verify it. # Action Detail 1 Create the rule New Data Access Rule scoping d_customers by region. 2 Assign to Manager Assign the rule to mgr_<prid> for their region. 3 Verify with User Access Summary Open User Access Summary for mgr_<prid> and confirm the rule and effective permissions are listed correctly.
documents.s: Part C — Data Access Rules & User Access Summary

documents.t: Simulate an incident requiring temporary elevated access, then audit it. # Action Detail 1 Grant temporary access Create a runtime Role Permission override allowing IT_TEAM_LEAD to Delete during an incident. 2 Use and revoke Apply, test the elevated Delete, then revoke the override. 3 Audit in Permission Logs Confirm both the grant and the revoke appear in Permission Logs with timestamp and actor. Session 3 Checkpoint ✔ CRUD restrictions enforced server-side for all 3 roles. ✔ IT Team row-level filtering confirmed, including via direct URL access. ✔ Data Access Rule created, assigned, and confirmed via User Access Summary. ✔ Temporary Role Permission granted, used, revoked, and fully audited in Permission Logs. Enhancement delivered: Replaces Level 1's UI-only button hiding (Vienable) with rules enforced at the platform/security level, restricts IT Team visibility to assigned complaints, scopes customer data by region, and closes the audit gap on temporary access.
documents.s: Part D — Role Permissions (Runtime) & Permission Logs

documents.t: Enable offline access to assigned complaints for field IT Team users via Local Archive. Reduce first-login sync payload using Initial Downloads. Push closed complaints to an external SAP system via Middleware. Bulk-import customer master data using KloSectionXlsx. What This Session Builds On The application has only worked online through Sessions 1–3. This session makes it usable by IT Team members working onsite without connectivity, and adds a bulk-data path for customer onboarding.

An IT Team technician visiting a customer site with no signal can't pull up the complaint they're there to resolve. Every login re-downloads the full complaint history instead of just what's assigned, closed complaints aren't reaching the SAP billing system automatically, and onboarding 20 new customers means entering each one by hand.

Keep a working slice of data on the device for offline use. # Action Detail 1 Configure archive scope Local Archive on d_complaints and d_complaint_voices for the IT_TEAM role — retain the last 30 days of assigned complaints on-device. 2 Test offline On a device/emulator, disconnect network and confirm assigned complaints and their voice history are still viewable.

Reduce what gets pulled on first login. # Action Detail 1 Configure the download set Only OPEN/INPROCESS complaints assigned to the logging-in IT Team user are included in the first sync — not full history. 2 Verify Time a fresh login before and after the change and confirm a smaller payload.

Integrate with an external billing system. # Action Detail 1 Configure the channel New Middleware channel that pushes CLOSED complaints to an external SAP endpoint for billing reconciliation. 2 Test Close a test complaint and confirm the outbound payload appears in the middleware queue.

Add Excel-based bulk operations to the customer master entity. # Action Detail 1 Add to d_customers Attach KloSectionXlsx to the customer section, enabling bulk Excel upload/download. 2 Bulk import Prepare a sample sheet of 20 customers and import via the section. 3 Verify Confirm all 20 records land correctly in Data Browser. Session 4 Checkpoint ✔ IT Team can view assigned complaints and voice history fully offline. ✔ Initial download payload measurably reduced and verified. ✔ One closed complaint confirmed pushed to the SAP middleware queue. ✔ 20 customers successfully bulk-imported via KloSectionXlsx. Enhancement delivered: Makes the app usable in the field without connectivity, shrinks the first-login sync payload, automates the SAP billing hand-off on closure, and adds bulk customer onboarding.
documents.s: Part D — KloSectionXlsx — Bulk Customer Import

documents.t: Route escalated complaints through a Manager approval Workflow. Add a nightly Scheduled Task as a server-side safety net for SLA breaches. Notify the right people by Email, SMS, and In-App at the right moments. Deep-link notification emails directly into the relevant complaint. Configure an app-wide Banner for planned maintenance. What This Session Builds On Session 1 added a server-side is_escalated flag. This session adds the human workflow and communication layer that reacts to it.

A complaint sits open for a week past SLA with no one following up, because there's no approval step and no nightly check catching it. A customer is never told their complaint was resolved unless someone remembers to call, and a support email can't deep-link straight to the complaint it's about.

Give escalation a human decision point. # Action Detail 1 Build the workflow When is_escalated becomes true, route an approval task to the Manager to confirm reassignment of responsible_team. 2 Test Trigger escalation on a test complaint and confirm the Manager receives the task in Pending Approvals.

Add a server-side safety net independent of individual saves. # Action Detail 1 Create the task Scheduled Task that runs nightly, re-checking all OPEN/INPROCESS complaints against the 3-day SLA rule from Session 1. 2 Run manually and verify Trigger once via Running Tasks and confirm overdue complaints are correctly flagged.
documents.s: Part B — Scheduler — Nightly SLA Sweep

documents.t: Close the communication loop for assignment and resolution. # Action Detail 1 Assignment email Email notification to responsible_team the moment a complaint is assigned. 2 Resolution in-app alert In-App notification to the originating Employee when status changes to CLOSED. 3 Verify delivery Trigger both scenarios and confirm delivery in Notification History.

Make notifications actionable and announce planned downtime. # Action Detail 1 Configure deeplink The assignment email's ‘View Complaint’ link opens directly to the correct complaint detail screen. 2 Configure Banner App-wide banner announcing a planned maintenance window, visible to all roles for 24 hours. Session 5 Checkpoint ✔ Escalation approval task correctly routed to and actionable by the Manager. ✔ Nightly scheduler flags overdue complaints on a manual run. ✔ Assignment email and resolution in-app alert both confirmed delivered in Notification History. ✔ Deeplink opens the exact correct complaint; banner visible to all 3 roles. Enhancement delivered: Adds a human approval step on escalation, a nightly check independent of individual saves, closes the communication loop on assignment/resolution, and makes notifications actionable.

Replace static dashboard tiles with a live kloChart. Build an advanced TAT trend chart over a rolling 30-day window. Build a Pivot Modeller report for cross-team, cross-type analysis. What This Session Builds On Level 1 Session 5 built p_complaint_dashboard with static status-count tiles fed by status_count_query. This session replaces and extends those same tiles with real charts.

A Manager glances at the dashboard and sees numbers that were already stale this morning, with no way to see the SLA trend over the last month or drill into which team is falling behind — only static totals.

Turn the existing tile counts into a live chart. # Action Detail 1 Add the chart Add a kloChart bar chart to p_complaint_dashboard bound to the existing status_count_query TransNode. 2 Cross-check and replace Verify the chart's counts match the old static tiles, then remove the tiles.

Add a second, more advanced chart tracking service-level performance. # Action Detail 1 Build the query New query aggregating actual_tat vs standard_tat by week for the last 30 days. 2 Configure the chart Advanced line chart with two series (actual vs standard) and custom axis formatting.
documents.s: Part B — Advanced Chart — TAT Trend

documents.t: Give Managers a drillable cross-tab report. # Action Detail 1 Build the pivot Rows = complaint_type, Columns = responsible_team, Values = count of complaints, Filter = current month. 2 Publish & verify Publish to the EAM Portal and confirm a Manager can drill into a specific cell to see the underlying records. Session 6 Checkpoint ✔ Static dashboard tiles fully replaced by a live kloChart with matching counts. ✔ TAT trend chart renders 30 days of actual-vs-standard data. ✔ Pivot report published to EAM Portal and drill-down verified. Enhancement delivered: Replaces static dashboard tiles with live, trend-aware reporting and adds a drillable cross-tab view for Managers.

Diagnose a simulated scheduler failure end-to-end using platform monitoring tools. Confirm notification delivery and resolve a stuck offline sync record. Confirm the SAP middleware payload was processed via Legacy Queue Monitoring. Trace a native control rendering issue on a built APK. Independently verify dashboard numbers using Query Console. What This Session Builds On The app is feature-complete after Sessions 1–6 (automation, offline sync, integrations, reporting). This session is entirely about operating and troubleshooting what was built, not adding new features.

The nightly SLA sweep silently failed last night and nobody noticed until complaints started piling up unflagged. A customer insists they never got a resolution notification, and there's no way to check; finance says a closed complaint never showed up in SAP and nobody can tell whether it's stuck or lost.

Break the Session 5 scheduler on purpose, then find and fix it. # Action Detail 1 Simulate a failure Introduce a bad condition into the nightly SLA-sweep task and trigger it. 2 Observe the failure Confirm the failure appears in Scheduler Monitoring and Task History. 3 Trace the root cause Find the underlying error in Google Logs. 4 Fix and re-run Correct the task and confirm success via Running Tasks.

Confirm the Session 4 and 5 integrations are actually working end-to-end. # Action Detail 1 Verify notifications Check Notification History for the assignment/resolution messages from Session 5 — confirm delivered status. 2 Diagnose a stuck sync Simulate a stuck offline record on Server Queue / Mobile Sync Queue for an IT Team device from Session 4, and resolve it. 3 Check the SAP channel Review Legacy Queue Monitoring to confirm the Session 4 closed-complaint payload to SAP was processed.

Trace a native rendering issue and cross-verify reporting data. # Action Detail 1 Build and test the APK Build a debug APK including the kloRating control from Session 2. 2 Debug if needed If the control fails to render natively, use APK/IPA debugging tools to trace the issue. 3 Cross-verify dashboard data Use Query Console to independently confirm the raw row counts behind the Session 6 dashboard charts. Session 7 Checkpoint ✔ Simulated scheduler failure diagnosed via Scheduler Monitoring + Google Logs and resolved. ✔ Notification delivery confirmed; one stuck sync record identified and resolved. ✔ SAP payload confirmed processed in Legacy Queue Monitoring. ✔ APK rendering issue for kloRating traced (fixed or root-caused). ✔ Dashboard chart numbers cross-verified against raw data via Query Console. Enhancement delivered: Shifts the training from building features to operating and troubleshooting everything Sessions 1–6 put in place.

Create a client-specific child flavor using App Inheritance. Customize the child flavor without touching the base app via App Modification. Apply Customer Branding to the login page, menus, and headers. Version-control all Level 2 code in a Git repo. Migrate the fully enhanced application to QA and confirm every enhancement survived. What This Session Builds On The base Customer Complaints app is now feature-rich after Sessions 1–7. This final session prepares it for a real client rollout — a branded, inherited child flavor, migrated to QA.

The business is onboarding a new client, Acme, who needs their own complaint categories and branded login screen without touching the shared base app every other client depends on. Before go-live, someone has to confirm a departed developer's session is revoked and that the whole app still works correctly once it's moved to QA.

Create a client-specific variant without duplicating the whole app. # Action Detail 1 Create the child flavor New flavor customer_complaints_acme_<prid> inheriting from the base application. 2 Override safely Use App Modification to override complaint_type values for Acme's business categories, without changing the base flavor.

Make the child flavor visually distinct. # Action Detail 1 Update login/registration Modify the index file for the Acme child flavor with Acme's logo and welcome text. 2 Apply CSS Style menus and headers to match Acme's brand colors, scoped to .procify__customer_complaints_acme_<prid>.

Clean up before go-live. # Action Detail 1 Push code to Git Push all entity rules, controller code, and CSS written across Sessions 1–8 into a Git repo. 2 Review sessions Check Active Sessions for the app and revoke any stale developer sessions before go-live.
documents.s: Part C — Git Repo & Active Sessions

documents.t: Ship the enhanced application and prove every feature survived the move. # Action Detail 1 Release the flavor Release the Acme child flavor. 2 Migrate Run App Migration (Transport) from DEV to QA. 3 Full smoke test On QA, verify: escalation rule (S1), embedded timeline (S2), permissions/row-level auth (S3), offline sync (S4), workflow + notifications (S5), dashboard charts (S6), and Acme branding (S8) all work correctly. Session 8 Checkpoint ✔ Acme child flavor created, visually distinct, and functionally overridden without touching the base app. ✔ All Level 2 code version-controlled in Git. ✔ Stale developer sessions reviewed and revoked. ✔ Application migrated to QA with every Session 1–8 enhancement verified working end-to-end. Enhancement delivered: Delivers a branded, client-specific flavor without touching the shared base app, and proves every Session 1–8 enhancement survives the move to QA.
documents.s: Part D — App Migration to QA

documents.t: Training Guide **Beginner** Date of Issue: 2025 Target Audience: Application Developers, Trainees. A Training Manual for application creation, knowledge and work reference. Training Procedure Welcome to the Procify Developer Training. This section explains the overall structure of the course, how sessions are designed, and what is expected of you as a trainee. Read this before starting Session 1. Course Structure — 8 Sessions​ The training spans 8 sessions. Each session introduces a new layer of the platform — starting with setup and ending with publishing a fully working application. Sessions must be taken in order; each one builds directly on the previous. Session Topic Session 1 Platform Setup & Account Management Session 2 BOL — Entity Fundamentals & Initial Pages Session 3 Entity Configuration (Relations, Object Types, Status, ID Series) Session 4 Value Helps & Queries Session 5 BOL Logic & Validations with dashboard creation Session 6 Bindings, Navigation & Styling Session 7 Controllers & Client-Side Behaviour Session 8 Menu Configuration & App Management, Versioning & Publishing The Learn-by-Building Approach​ This training does not teach concepts in isolation. You will build one real application — a Customer complaint system — across all 89 sessions. Every concept is introduced exactly when you need it to make the next part of that application work. Why this matters for you You will always know WHY you are doing each step, not just HOW. By Session 8 you will have a working application demonstrating every major platform capability. The application grows session by session — if you miss a step it will affect later sessions. When you encounter a similar situation on a real project, you will have a concrete reference point from training.

Attend each session with the previous session's assignment completed and verified. Follow steps in this guide during hands-on time — do not skip ahead. Ask questions during the Review & Q&A phase, not during the trainer demonstration. The Application You Will Build This training guide uses a REAL application: the Customer complaints Application. You are not building a demo — you are building a production-ready application for delivery personnel. Every concept taught in every session is applied directly to build this application. By Session 9 you will have a fully working, published Delivery Agent Application.

Session Objectives​ By the end of this session, we will be able to: Understand the platform architecture. Create an application in the Workspace Hub. Define application roles and understand system vs. application roles. Create user accounts and assign them to an application with the correct role. Use Team Groups (User collections) to bundle multiple users and assign them to an application in a single, bulk step. Understands the role of data studio and page builder in application creation. ⚠ Why this session comes first The App you create today is built across ALL 9 sessions — treat it carefully. The Roles you define today are referenced in Session 5 (Validations) and Session 9 (Publishing access). The Users you create today are the test personas you will use to verify every screen built in Sessions 2–8. Part A — Understanding the Customer complaint Application​ Before touching any tool, you need a clear picture of the application you are building. Read this section carefully — every configuration decision in Sessions 1– traces back to this Business Requirement Document. Application Purpose​ The Customer Complaints Application is a solution designed to manage customer complaints end-to-end across three personas: • Log and track customer complaints with full lifecycle management. • Route complaints from Employee → Manager → Responsible Team. • Manage complaint line items, voice records, and file attachments. • Monitor escalations, SLA (TAT), and resolution timelines. • Provide dashboards per role so every user sees what they need. Application Roles — Three Personas​ This application defines exactly three application roles, each mapped to a Procify role-rollup level for viewable and UI-Auth controls: Role ID Business Name Procify Role Rollup Employee Complaint Creator Owner (s_role_rollup = 10) Manager Complaint Assignor Supervisor (s_role_rollup = 20) Responsible Team Issue Resolver Reviewer (s_role_rollup = 30) 📘 Role Precedence Rule Precedence is a number. Lower = higher priority. Employee: precedence 3, Manager: precedence 2, ResponsibleTeam: precedence 1. This means if a user has multiple roles, the lower-precedence number overrides. Your developer account should be assigned Manager (precedence 2) for full access during testing. Role Responsibilities​ Action Employee(Owner) Manager(Supervisor) Responsible Team(Reviewer) Create a new complaint ✅ Yes — — View own complaints ✅ Yes ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Edit complaint description ✅ Yes (OPEN only) ✅ Yes — Assign responsible team — ✅ Yes — Move status → INPROCESS — ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Move status → ON HOLD — — ✅ Yes Move status → RESOLVED — ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Move status → CLOSED ✅ Yes ✅ Yes — Reopen a closed complaint ✅ Yes ✅ Yes — Add complaint items ✅ Yes (OPEN/INPROCESS) — — Add voice/comment records ✅ Yes ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Upload attachments ✅ Yes ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Escalate complaint ✅ Yes ✅ Yes — View all complaints (not just own) — ✅ Yes ✅ Yes (assigned) Entities to be Built​ Entity ID Primary Key Built in Session d_complaints complaint_id Session 1 d_complaint_item item_id Session 2 d_complaint_voices voice_id Session 2 d_complaints_attachment attachment_id Session 2 d_customers customer_id Session 2 d_resp_team emp_id Session 2 Complaint Status Flow​ The status lifecycle has 6 states. Each transition is triggered by a specific role: OPEN INPROCESS ON HOLD RESOLVED CLOSED REOPEN ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ Triggered by Employee Triggered by Manager / Responsible Team Triggered by Responsible Team Triggered by Responsible Team / Manager Triggered by Manager / Employee Triggered by Employee / Manager Status Badge Colour / Meaning OPEN Blue — complaint logged by Employee, awaiting Manager assignment INPROCESS Orange — Manager assigned responsible team; team working on it ON HOLD Purple — Responsible Team placed on hold pending information RESOLVED Green — Responsible Team marked as resolved CLOSED Grey — Manager confirmed resolution and closed the ticket REOPEN Red — Employee or Manager reopened a resolved/closed complaint 📘 Status Transition Rules OPEN → INPROCESS: only Manager can trigger (by assigning responsible_team).INPROCESS → ON HOLD / RESOLVED: only ResponsibleTeam can trigger.RESOLVED → CLOSED: only Manager can trigger.CLOSED → REOPEN: Employee or Manager can reopen; status resets to OPEN.ON HOLD → INPROCESS: only ResponsibleTeam can resume. d_complaint — Propertiesplaints — All Properties Property ID Data Type Key Attr Notes complaint_id String 🔑 PK Auto-generated via ID Series — e.g. CMP-00001 complaint_desc Text ❗ Mandatory Full description of the complaint customer_id String — FK → d_customers.customer_id priority String — Values: Low / Medium / High / Critical status string — Status of the ticket. first_response_date Timestamp — Date of first response to customer planned_resolution_date Timestamp — Planned closure date assigned_to String — Employee user ID who owns the complaint responsible_manager String — FK → d_sales_team.emp_id — Manager assigned responsible_team String — Team assigned by Manager for resolution remark Text — Internal remarks or resolution notes closed_on Timestamp — Date the complaint was closed is_escalated Boolean — Default: false — true if escalated by Manager complaint_type String — Type classification of the complaint nature_of_complaint String — Nature/category of the complaint actual_tat Decimal — Actual turnaround time in days standard_tat Decimal — SLA turnaround time in days created_on Timestamp — Audit: auto-set on creation created_by String — Audit: user who created the record modified_on Timestamp — Audit: auto-updated on every save modified_by String — Audit: user who last modified the record d_complaint_item — Properties​ Property ID Data Type Key Attr Notes item_id String 🔑 PK Primary key — auto-generated ticket_id String — FK → d_complaints.complaint_id product String ❗ Mandatory Product name related to the complaint item issue_observed Text — Description of the issue observed d_complaint_voices — Properties​ Property ID Data Type Key Attr Notes voice_id String 🔑 PK Primary key — auto-generated ticket_id String — FK → d_complaints.complaint_id customer String — Customer providing the voice/comment responsible_team String — Team responsible for this voice record sales_manager String — FK → d_sales_team.emp_id d_complaints_attachment — Properties​ Property ID Data Type Key Attr Notes attachment_id String 🔑 PK Primary key — auto-generated complaint_id String — FK → d_complaints.complaint_id attachment Binary / Blob — Actual attachment file content attachment_type String — MIME type or file type classification d_customers — Properties​ Property ID Data Type Key Attr Notes customer_id String 🔑 PK Unique customer identifier customer_name String ❗ Mandatory Full name of the customer customer_type String — Individual / Corporate / Distributor d_resp_team — Properties​ Property ID Data Type Key Attr Notes emp_id String 🔑 PK Employee ID — unique identifier name String ❗ Mandatory Full name of the sales team member Entity Relationships​ Relationship Detail d_complaints → d_complaint_item One Complaint → Many Items. d_complaint_item.ticket_id → d_complaints.complaint_id (Primary Relation — child of BO) d_complaints → d_complaint_voices One Complaint → Many Voices. d_complaint_voices.ticket_id → d_complaints.complaint_id (Primary Relation — child of BO) d_complaints → d_complaints_attachment One Complaint → Many Attachments. d_complaints_attachment.complaint_id → d_complaints.complaint_id (Primary Relation — child of BO) d_complaints → d_customers One Customer → Many Complaints. d_complaints.customer_id → d_customers.customer_id (Non-Primary Relation) Pages to be Built​ Screen ID Purpose p_home_page Home Page — summary tiles (Open count, Escalated count, Resolved Today), quick actions, and recent complaints list. Content adapts per role. p_complaints Complaint Management — list, search, and full detail view with tabs for items, voices, and attachments. Menu Structure​ Menu Item Screen Icon Visible to Complaints p_complaints sap-icon://customer-and-contacts All roles Naming Convention for This Training​ Item Convention App ID customer_complaints_<your_prid> e.g. customer_complaints_pr0045 Display Name Customer Complaints Application — <Your Name> Role 1 (Creator) Employee (precedence: 3) Role 2 (Assignor) Manager (precedence: 2) Role 3 (Resolver) ResponsibleTeam (precedence: 1) Test User (Employee) emp_<your_prid> e.g. emp_pr0045 Test User (Manager) mgr_<your_prid> e.g. mgr_pr0045 Test User (Resolver) res_<your_prid> e.g. res_pr0045 ⚠ Naming Rules App ID must be unique across the landscape — use your PRID to avoid collisions. Use only lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores. No spaces, hyphens, or special characters. The App ID cannot be changed after creation. ​ Part B — Workspace Hub: Users​ Reference: Workspace Hub 7.0 - User Guide Workspace Hub is an Admin Tool that focuses on managing applications and the application users. It is a versatile application that serves diverse purposes from user management to application management. Apart from that, this tool can also be used for modifying the already existing users and apps. Navigating to the Workspace Hub​ Workspace Hub menu will be visible for Users who are assigned as TESTER or DEVELOPER or SUPERADMIN for cockpit flavor. Step 1: Go to the menu options and select Workspace Hub. Step 2: The Workspace Hub contains the following Pages. What Is a User?​ A User is a platform-level account — a person who can log in to one or more applications. Users exist independently of applications. You create the person first, then assign them to applications with roles separately. The same user can have different roles in different applications. Creating a New User​ Create one test user to represent the end-user persona (emp01) throughout all sessions. 1 Navigate to Users In the Workspace Hub, click Users in the left navigation. The user list screen loads. 2 Click Create New User Click the create button in the toolbar. 3 Fill in User Details Complete all required fields as shown in the table below. Field What to enter Title Choose the title from dropdown (Mandatory) First Name Fill the first name (Mandatory) Last Name Fill the last name (Optional) Email A real or placeholder email address (Mandatory) Mobile Number used for OTP login if configured (Mandatory) Designation Fill the designation (Mandatory) User ID (Login ID) test_<your_prid> e.g. test_pr0045 BPID Choose bpid from dropdown (Mandatory) Authcode Choose authcode from dropdown (Mandatory) 4 Save the User Click Save. The user is created. Note the User ID — you will reference it when assigning this user to the application. Important — User Created ≠ User Has Access Creating a user only adds them to the platform's user directory. They cannot access any application until assigned to one with a specific role. You will complete that assignment in Part D of this session. If a user tries to log in before assignment, they will see error mentioning no applications assigned Refer Create User part from workspace hub manual for more information. Part C — Workspace Hub: Apps & Roles​ What Is an Application in Klobase?​ An application is a self-contained unit that holds all the metadata you build — entities, queries, pages, menus, and more. It is the primary organising structure of everything you will do in Sessions 2–8. Users are assigned to applications (with roles), not to individual Pages or features. Creating the Customer complaint Application​ 1 Navigate to Apps In the Workspace Hub, click Apps in the left navigation. 2 Click Create New App Click the Add button. The application creation form opens. 3 Fill in Application Details Complete the fields as shown in the table below. Field What to enter App ID Change the App ID according to the application App Name Same as app id Description (optional) Service Request Management training application 4 Save the Application Click Save. The app appears in the Apps list with Active status. Understanding Roles​ Roles control what a user can do inside the application. Procify has two categories: Role Type What it controls System Roles (built-in) MANAGER,DEVELOPER and TESTER— control access to dev tools (data studio,page builder, Workspace Hub, Private Node). Pre-built into the platform. Application Roles (custom) Roles you define inside your app. Control what users see and can do at runtime within your app's Pages and data. For this training, define single application role inside your app: Role Name Precedence Role Name DeliveryAgent 1 DeliveryAgent Role Precedence — Key Rule Precedence is a number. Lower number = higher priority. If a user has multiple roles, the one with the lowest precedence number takes effect at runtime. Delivery Admin(1) always overrides Delivery Agent(2) for a user assigned both roles. Your developer account will be Delivery Admin. The test user will be SRM_User. This lets you test both personas. Part E — understanding the importance of Procify​ Every application starts the same way: someone hands a developer a requirements document and says 'build this.' The Customer complaints Application Business Requirement Document (BRD) you read in Session 1 defines exactly what data needs to be stored — 3 data objects, their fields, and their relationships. The first job as a developer is to turn those definitions into a working database schema. Before opening any tool, it is worth understanding what that process looks like — and how much of it Procify eliminates. The rest of this part walks through the traditional process step by step, then shows exactly which steps the data studio replaces. What Is a Schema?​ 📘 Schema — The Blueprint of Your Application's Data A schema is the complete definition of the data your application stores: what tables exist, what columns each table has, what type of data each column holds, and how tables relate to each other. The schema is the foundation of every application. Without it, there is no database. Without a database, there is no data. Without data, there is no application. Building the schema is always the first development task after reading a BRD. Everything else — APIs, Pages, logic — is built on top of it. In our BRD, the schema is already defined in Section 4 (Entity Relationship Overview). The 4 entities, their properties, and their relationships are all there. Our job today is to implement that schema. The Traditional Way of Building a Schema​ 🏗 How developers build a schema without a low-code platform Step 1 — Write SQL scripts: A backend developer writes CREATE TABLE statements for each entity. For the Delivery table alone, that is 12 columns — each with its SQL data type, constraints, default values, and indexes. Step 2 — Write an ORM model: For every SQL table, the developer writes a model class in the backend language (Node.js/TypeScript, Python, Java). This class mirrors the database table and handles object-relational mapping. Step 3 — Write REST API endpoints: For each entity, the developer writes GET, POST, PUT, DELETE API handlers. Each handler validates input, maps it to the model, executes the database query, and returns the response. Step 4 — Write validation logic: For each property that has rules (mandatory, unique, min/max), the developer writes validation code — either in the model or in the API handler. Step 5 — Handle database migrations: Every time the schema changes (new property, renamed column), the developer writes a migration script to alter the existing tables without losing data. Step 6 — Test the API: The developer uses Postman or writes unit tests to verify each endpoint returns the correct data in the correct format. Repeat for all 4 entities. 🔴 The pain of the traditional approach Multiple files across multiple layers — SQL files, model files, API controller files, test files. A change to one field requires edits in 4–6 places. Context switching: a single developer must switch between SQL, backend language, API design, and test writing — each requiring a different mental mode. Time cost: 3–4 days of developer time before a single screen can be shown to a stakeholder. Repetition: most of this work is identical boilerplate — every entity needs the same pattern of SQL + ORM + CRUD APIs. Nothing creative, just repetitive. ​ The Procify Way​ ✅ How Procifyreplaces the traditional schema-building process In Klobase, all 6 traditional steps are replaced by a single tool: the data studio. You define the entity (name, type) → add properties (name, data type, key attributes) → click Update Schema. Done. The platform automatically generates: the database table (SQL step 1), the data access layer (ORM step 2), the REST API endpoints (step 3), basic validation from key attributes (step 4), and handles schema updates automatically (step 5). There are no separate files to keep in sync. The data studio is the single source of truth. Everything downstream — API, data validation, mobile sync — is derived from it automatically. Time with Klobase: the same 4 entities, all properties, schema live in the database — approximately 2 hours in this session. The developer's time is freed for the parts that actually require thinking: business logic, UI design, user experience. This is not an approximation. Let us make it concrete: Traditional Task data studio Replacement Write CREATE TABLE SQL for Delivery entity Create entity in data studio — choose type, add properties, click Save Write ORM model class (12 fields × 4 entities) Already done — properties ARE the model Write 16+ REST API endpoints Already done — fireQuery apis are available to fetch data Write validation for mandatory fields Check the Mandatory key attribute icon on the property and validation will be handled by platform. Write database migration script Click Update Schema again — the platform handles ALTER TABLE automatically Test APIs with Postman Use the built-in Test function in the data studio toolbar ​ The Traditional Way of Building a UI​ 🔴 Traditional screen development requires five separate layers 1. HTML / JSX template — the visual structure: list container, card component, placeholder slots for each field. 2. CSS / styling — card appearance, status badge colours, spacing, responsiveness for mobile and desktop. 3. API call — GET /complaints?user={currentUser.id} to fetch complaint records from the server. 4. State management (React state, Redux, etc.) — store the fetched array, handle loading state, handle error state, trigger re-renders when data changes. 5. Data binding — map each complaint object's fields to the template slots: {complaint.complaint_desc}, {complaint.priority}. Total: 3–5 files, 150–300 lines of code, for one list screen. Any change to one layer often requires changes to the others. The Procify Way — The Page Wizard & Page Builder​ ✅ The Page Builder replaces all five layers with a single metadata configuration In the Page Builder you configure the screen structure. The platform reads your configuration and generates the visual rendering, handles all data fetching, manages state automatically, applies your styling choices, and wires up the data bindings. This means: one tool, no files to keep in sync, no merge conflicts on screen structure, no state management code. The Page Wizard (used in this session) gives you a ready-made screen in minutes. Session 2 teaches you to build the same screen step-by-step so you understand every level of the hierarchy. Pages configured in the Page Builder render identically on both browser (web) and mobile (KloTouch) — no separate mobile codebase needed. B.3 — The Page Hierarchy (UI Editor 7.0 User Guide — Sections 3.0–7.0)​ Every screen in Klobase follows a strict 5-level hierarchy. This is the most important structural concept in UI development. Each level has a mandatory naming convention prefix: 📘 Five-Level Page Hierarchy Level 1 — PAGE (prefix: p_) The root container. Holds all layouts. Created first. One page can have multiple layouts (one per device type). At runtime, the platform picks the layout based on device: screencontainerdesktop, screencontainermobile, screencontainertab, screencontainerdefault. Level 2 — PAGE LAYOUT (prefix: pl_) Sits directly under the Page. Defines HOW the page areas are arranged. screenType options: stack, tab, two_column, object_page, grid_layout, hsplitter, vsplitter. Example: pl_complaints_desk (two column layout for desktop). Level 3 — PAGE AREA (prefix: pa_) A logical sub-container inside the layout. Can itself have a screenType (tab, stack, splitter). Sections are assigned to page areas to determine WHERE they render. Example: pa_complaints (list area), pa_complaint_details (detail area). Level 4 — SECTION (prefix: s_) The rendering unit. screenType determines HOW it displays data. Types: search, cardlist, card, form, grid, tree, timeline, map, calendar. Must be assigned to a Page Area to appear in the UI. Example: s_search (search), s_complaints (grid), s_detail_header (form). Level 5 — CONTROLS Individual fields, buttons, labels, icons bound to entity properties. Added via: right-click section → New → Controls, OR drag from unused TransNode properties. Section screenType Renders As search Filter bar with Close / Reset / Search buttons. Auto-generates the search toolbar. cardlist List of records as card rows — one card per record. Good for mobile and compact lists. grid Tabular list with column headers and rows. Supports sort, filter, group-by per column. form Detail form layout. Each control renders as a labelled input field. card Single entity rendered as a CSS grid card. One record only. tab Used on Page Areas to group child sections as tabs. showTitle must be true for tab labels. tree Hierarchical tree display for nested data. B.4 — Page Data Model (TransNodes) — Concept​ The Page Data Model defines the data available to a screen. Every section and control that displays data must be bound to a TransNode. A TransNode is a “data pipe” — it fetches entity records from the database and makes them available to sections and controls on the page. Node Type Fetches EntitySet A LIST of records. Use for search sections, grids, card lists. Suffix convention: _list. Example: d_complaints_list Entity ONE record (the currently selected record). Use for detail forms. Suffix convention: _detail. Example: d_complaints_detail Query Records from a kloQuery with WHERE conditions, joins, sorting. Suffix convention: _query. This is the mechanism that connects list → detail. Without Fold From: the detail section will always be empty.
