Save after each set. 📘 s_search Controls — Match the Search Bar in the Screenshot Row 1: complaint_id (Ticket Id text input), s_status, complaint_type Row 2: desc (Description text input), is_escalated (Escalated checkbox), nature_of_compl Row 3: customer_id (Employee ID — with Value Help picker icon), cust_category (Employee, actual_tat (Actual TAT number input) Row 4: priority, cust_type , standard_tat (Standard TAT number input) Tree also shows: raised_by, state, cust_category_lbl, cust_type_lbl (label controls for display) How to add controls via drag-and-drop (UI Editor 7.0 Guide — Section 2.2.6 DnD on Preview): 1. In the Page Data Model panel, select search→ click Unused Properties tab. 2. Drag any property from the unused list and drop it onto s_search in the tree. 3. The control is created automatically with the property binding pre-set. 4. You can drag and drop controls within the section to align the controls. 📸 Final Output — After Creating s_search Once s_search is created with all controls and you click Show Full Preview, you will see the search filter bar rendered at the top of the screen exactly as shown below. Expected output: s_search renders the Employee Complaints filter bar with all fields — Ticket Id, Status, Complaint Type, Escalated checkbox, Employee Category, Priority, Nature of Complaint, Actual TAT, and Standard TAT. Close / Reset / Search buttons are auto-generated by the search scr eenType. 📸 Tree View — How s_search Looks in the Page Builder Tree After adding all controls, s_search in the tree should look like the screenshot below. Each control is listed under the section with its entity property binding. Page Builder tree showing pa_complaints → s_search with all controls: ticket_id, desc, customer_id, responsible_tea, priority, s_status, is_escalated, cust_category_lbl, cust_category, cust_type_lbl, cust_type, complaint_type, raised_by, state, nature_of_compl, actual_tat, standard_tat B.9.2 — Creating the Complaints List Section (s_complaints)​ The grid section renders complaint records as rows with sortable, filterable columns. Per UI Editor 7.0 Guide (Section 6.2 — Grid): For desktop view, section screenType should be “grid”. Add a conf_grid000 config node for grid behaviour settings. 1 Right-click pa_complaints → New → Section. Rename: s_complaints. 2 In the Detail panel, set screenType = grid. 3 Set TransNode path = list. 4 Right-click pa_complaints → New → Assign → select s_complaints (below s_search). Save. 5 Add controls from d_complaints_list TransNode unused properties: ticket_id (set the control type as m.link and add press event with function as ‘navTo’(Fill the sunscreen id as detail page area) ), customer_id, priority, s_status, planned_res_dat, closed_on, sales_manager. 6 Right-click s_complaints → New → Config → rename: conf_grid000. This config node stores grid behaviour properties. 7 Right-click s_complaints → New → Toolbar. Add Add and Delete buttons in the toolbar detail. 8 Arrange the controls in s_complaints by using drag and drop feature inside section 9 Save. 📸 Final Output — After Creating s_complaint Once s_complaints is created with all controls and you click Show Full Preview, you will see the complaints list rendered below search section You can notice that the screen we created is not the same in the provided screenshot. Complaint_id contains id-desc Status has color Grid is occupying full screen Pont 1 & 2 will be achieved in the upcoming sessions. For point 3 we can achieve this by setting screentype of pa_complaints as fit_to_area and mark auto_height as true for s_complaints layout. 📸 Tree View — How s_complaints Looks in the Page Builder Tree After building s_complaints, it should appear in the tree as shown below — with ticket_id as a navigation link, all property controls, conf_grid000, and section_toolbar. Page Builder tree showing s_complaints with controls: ticket_id (link icon), customer_id, priority, s_status, planned_res_dat, closed_on, sales_manager, plus conf_grid000 config and section_toolbar B.10 — Step 5: Create the Detail Page Area (pa_complaint_details)​ The detail area loads when a complaint row is selected from the list. It contains a toolbar for actions, a header section showing critical fields, and a tabbed area for all complaint details. 1 Right-click pl_complaints_desk → New → Page Area. Rename: pa_complaint_details. 2 Update screentype as tab B.10.2 — Creating the Detail Header Section (s_detail_header)​ The header section displays the most critical complaint fields prominently. screenType: card. Bound to d_complaints_detail TransNode. 1 Right-click pa_complaint_details → New → Section. Rename: s_detail_header. 2 Set screenType = card. Set TransNode path = detail. 3 Add controls from d_complaints_detail unused properties: desc, s_status, priority, res_team, responsible_tea. ⇒ change the control to m.Text for making it readable only 4 Save. 📸 Final Output — After Creating s_detail_header Once s_detail_header is created with all controls and you click Show Full Preview, you will see the result as mentioned below after modeling which will be covered in upcoming sessions 📸 Tree View — How s_detail_header Looks in the Page Builder Tree After creating s_detail_header with all header controls, it should appear as shown below. Rename: pa_comp_details. 2 In the Detail panel, set screenType = default. Set showTitle = true & title = detail so tab labels are visible. 3 Assign the page area to pa_complaints_detail. 4 Now create all 4 sections inside pa_comp_details. Right-click pa_comp_details → New → Section for each. Set each to screenType = form Set TransNode = detail for form sections. 5 Set each section’s title property — this becomes the tab label visible at runtime. 5 Assign all 4 sections to pa_comp_details in the correct sequence. Save. 6 Set type = header for s_detail_header layout & type = section for pa_comp_details. 7 Set press event for complaint_id link with function as navTo => pageArea : pa_complaint_details. Close / Reset / Search buttons present. 4 Verify the complaint list appears below the search bar with columns: ticket_id (clickable link), customer_id, priority, status, planned resolution date, closed date. 5 Click a complaint row. Verify the detail area loads with the header section (description, status, priority) and the tab area below. 6 Navigate through each tab — Complaint Details, Assignment, Reporter Info, TAT & Timeline, Complaint Items. Verify correct fields in each. 7 If a section appears blank: select it in the tree and check that its TransNode path is correctly set in the Detail panel. documents.t: By the end of this session, you will be able to: Understand what Entity Relations are and create Primary and Non-Primary (Aggregated) relations between entities. Understand what Object Types are, why they are needed, and configure complaint type classifications for d_complaints. Configure Status and Status Groups to represent the complaint lifecycle (OPEN → INPROCESS → ON HOLD → RESOLVED → CLOSED → REOPEN). Set up an ID Series for complaint_id to auto-generate readable complaint numbers (e.g. CMP-00001). Update the p_complaints UI to reflect the new entity configuration — making the complaint_type, status, and complaint_id fields work correctly in the page. 📘 What This Session Builds On Session 1 created the application, roles, users, and d_complaints entity with raw properties. Session 2 created the remaining 5 entities and built the full p_complaints page step by step. Session 3 enriches the d_complaints entity with the platform features that turn raw fields into intelligent, lifecycle-aware data. After Session 3, the complaint_id will auto-generate, the status dropdown will show the correct lifecycle values, and complaint_type will be classified. Without a relation defined in the BOL Editor, the platform has no way to automatically load child records when a parent record is selected — and no way to bundle the BO for save/delete operations. There are two types of relations in Klobase: Relation Type What It Means Primary Relation Tight parent-child bond WITHIN the same Business Object (BO). A child entity is dependent on the parent. Prefixed pr_. Used for d_complaint_item, d_complaint_voices, d_complaints_attachment — all children of d_complaints. Non-Primary (Aggregated) Relation Looser link BETWEEN BOs. Used to reference standalone master entities. Prefixed r_. Used for d_customers and d_resp_team which are independent master entities. 📘 Why Relations Matter in the UI When a relation is defined and referenced in a TransNode in the Page Builder, the platform automatically fetches the child/linked entity records when the parent record is loaded. Without a relation, you would have to write manual queries and wire up the data fetch yourself. The TransNode type 'Relation' in the Page Data Model uses the relation name defined here — this is why naming the relation correctly matters. Naming convention (from BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Best Practices): pr_ prefix for primary relations, r_ prefix for associated/aggregated relations. Always lowercase. A.2 — Relations to Create for d_complaints​ You will create 5 relations on the d_complaints root entity — one for each related entity. Relation ID Type Return Entity Cardinality r_complaint_item Non-Primary (Aggregated) d_complaint_item 1:n (One complaint → Many items) r_complaint_voices Non-Primary (Aggregated) d_complaint_voices 1:n (One complaint → Many voices) r_complaint_attach Non-Primary (Aggregated) d_complaints_attachment 1:n (One complaint → Many attachments) r_customer Non-Primary (Aggregated) d_customers 1:1 (One complaint has one customer) r_resp_team Non-Primary (Aggregated) d_resp_team 1:1 (One complaint has one responsible team member) A.3 — Step-by-Step: Creating a Primary Relation​ Primary Relation will be automatically created with the creation of child entity and requires no manual action A.4 — Step-by-Step: Creating a Non-Primary (Aggregated) Relation​ Non-primary relations link d_complaints to standalone master entities (d_customers and d_resp_team). Follow these steps for r_customer # Action Detail 1 d_complaints Relations tab click d_complaints in the tree and go back to the Relations tab. 2 Click Add Click the Add (+) icon to add a new relation row. 3 Fill Relation Details Relation Name: r_customer 4 Configure Mapping Click Mapping. Add: Source Property = customer_id 5 Save Click Save. 💡 Mapping Type — BOTH Explained ON CREATE: When a new d_complaint_item is created under a d_complaints parent, the platform automatically copies the complaint_id value into the ticket_id field of the new item. You never have to set this manually. ON QUERY: When you query d_complaint_item records for a given complaint, the platform uses ticket_id = complaint_id as the WHERE condition automatically. BOTH: Use this for standard parent-child relations — it handles both the create and the fetch scenarios. Now repeat the same steps to create the remaining relations: Relation ID Return Entity Mapping (Source → Target) r_complaint_voices d_complaint_voices complaint_id → ticket_id r_complaint_items d_complaint_item complaint_id → ticket_id r_complaint_attach d_complaints_attachment complaint_id → complaint_id r_resp_team d_resp_team responsible_team → emp_id Part B — Configuring Object Types for d_complaints​ B.1 — What Is an Object Type?​ In Klobase, an Object Type (stored in the system property s_object_type) is a classification that tags each record as belonging to a specific type. Object Types serve two important purposes: They enable role-based visibility: a button or field can be made visible/editable only for a specific role AND a specific object type combination. This is used for screen behavior in Session 7. They allow ID Series to be object-type-specific: a different number series prefix can be applied per object type — for example, complaints created by Maventic employees might use a different prefix than those created by Procify employees. 📘 Object Type vs Object Group Object Group is a container that groups related Object Types together. The group is used as the filter boundary. Object Type is the actual tag applied to individual records (e.g. MAVENTIC, PROCIFY). Every Object Type must belong to exactly one Object Group. For the Customer Complaints application: Object Group = company_types Object Types = MAVENTIC, PROCIFY Best Practice (BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide): Always maintain an Object Group to group types — the same group can be used in default filters based on users. B.2 — Object Types for d_complaints​ Object Type ID Description MAVENTIC Complaints created by Maventic employees PROCIFY Complaints created by Procify employees B.3 — Step-by-Step: Creating Object Group and Object Types​ # Action Detail 1 Go to Object Type tab Select d_complaints in the tree. Click the Object Type tab in the Detail panel. The tab shows two sections: the upper section for Object Types 2 Open Object Group dialog In the Object Type section, click the dialog icon next to the Object Group field to open the Object Group management dialog. 3 Create Object Group In the Object Group dialog, click Add. Fill in: Object Group ID: complaint_types 4 Close dialog Click Cancel / Close on the Object Group dialog to return to the Object Type tab. 5 Add first Object Type Fill: Object Type: MAVENTIC 6 Add remaining types Repeat Add for: PROCIFY — under Object Group: complaint_types. Click Save after all are added. 7 Verify All Object Types appear in the list, all with Object Group: complaint_types. ​ After adding the object type to differentiate complaints based on company is only half in order to achieve difference in complaint_id based on company another part is pending which is configuring ID Series based on object_type. Part C — Setting Up ID Series for Auto-Numbering​ D.1 — What Is an ID Series?​ An ID Series is a platform-managed counter that automatically generates primary key values when a new record is created. Without an ID Series on complaint_id, a developer would need to generate unique IDs manually — which is error-prone and cannot produce readable, formatted numbers like CMP-00001. ID Series Type Description Auto Number Returns an incrementing number. Combined with a Prefix pattern to produce CMP-00001, CMP-00002, etc. GUID Returns a 32-character UUID. Good for distributed offline scenarios. Not human-readable. None No auto-generation. The developer or rule must set the key manually. D.2 — ID Series to Configure​ Property Type Company Pattern/Prefix Start From complaint_id Auto Number PROCIFY Prefix: P- (generates P-00001) 1 complaint_id Auto Number MAVENTIC Prefix: M - (generates M-00001) 1 D.3 — Step-by-Step: Creating the ID Series​ # Action Detail 1 Select d_complaints In the Data Studio tree, click on d_complaints. 2 Go to Properties tab Click the Properties tab in the Detail panel. Locate the complaint_id property row. 3 Open ID Series Click the navigation right arrow (→) at the end of the complaint_id row. The ID Series dialog opens for this property. 4 Click Add Click the Add (+) icon in the ID Series dialog. A new entry row appears. 5 Fill ID Series details ID: idp_complaint 6 Click Add Click the Add (+) icon in the ID Series dialog. A new entry row appears. 7 Fill ID Series details ID: idm_complaint 8 Close dialog Click Close on the dialog. The ID Series entry is saved. 9 Save Click Save in the Data Studio toolbar. The complaint_id property now has an ID Series configured. 📘 ID Series Fields Reference (BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 3.0.1 Creating ID Series) ID: Unique ID of the series. Naming convention: id_ prefix, all lowercase. Example: id_complaint. Type: Auto Number = incremental counter. Most common for business records. From: Starting number for the series. Use 1 to start from P-00001. Prefix: Text prepended before the number. P- produces P-1, P-2, etc. Chunk Size: Default 100. The server pre-allocates this many IDs per session (important for offline apps). Scope: Global (default) — one counter shared across all users and tenants. Pattern: Can be used to produce complex formats. For simple prefix + number, just use the Prefix field. D.4 — Testing the ID Series​ # Action Detail 1 Open Data Browser With d_complaints selected, click Test in the toolbar. The Data Browser opens. 2 Create a new record Click Add (+ Execute → Add → select object_type). Leave complaint_id blank — the platform will fill it. 3 Fill minimal fields complaint_desc: Test auto-number 4 Verify The complaint_id column should show P-00001 for Procify and M-0001 for Maventic (or the next available number). If it shows a blank or an error, revisit the ID Series configuration. Part C — Configuring Status and Status Groups​ C.1 — What Is Status in Klobase?​ The system property s_status represents the current state of a complaint record. The Status tab in the Data Studio lets you define the allowed values for s_status and group them into Status Groups. Status Groups are named collections of statuses. They are used in Vienable (Session 7) to control screen behaviour: for example, the Edit button is visible only when s_status is in the OPEN_GROUP, and the Assign Team button is visible only when s_status is in the INPROCESS_GROUP. 📘 Status Lifecycle for Customer Complaints The complaint lifecycle defined in the BRD has 6 states: OPEN → INPROCESS → ON_HOLD / RESOLVED → CLOSED / REOPEN Each status transition is triggered by a specific role (defined in the Role Responsibility matrix from Session 1 Part A). In this session you define the status values and groups. The actual UI enforcement of transitions using Vienable happens in Session 7. C.2 — Status Values and Groups to Configure​ Status ID Short Label Status Group Triggered By OPEN Open OPEN Auto-set on complaint creation by Employee INPROCESS In Process INPROCESS Manager assigns responsible_team ON_HOLD On Hold INPROCESS Responsible Team puts on hold RESOLVED Resolved ACCEPTED Responsible Team / Manager marks resolved CLOSED Closed COMPLETED Manager confirms resolution and closes REOPEN Re-Opened OPEN Employee or Manager reopens a closed complaint C.3 — Step-by-Step: Adding Status Values​ # Action Detail 1 Go to Status tab Select d_complaints in the tree. Click the Status tab in the Detail panel. 2 Enable Switch on the status and click save and edit 3 Add OPEN status Click the Add Record(+) icon. Fill: Status: OPEN 4 Add remaining statuses Repeat Add for each status: INPROCESS (In Process), ON_HOLD (On Hold), RESOLVED (Resolved), CLOSED (Closed), REOPEN (Re-Opened) for PROCIFY. Click Save after all are added. Repeat for MAVENTIC Repeat the Action 3 and 4 for object_type maventic as well. 4 Verify list All 12 status values appear in the status list. 💡 Why Status Groups Are Important for This Application Session 7 will use these groups to configure Vienable on buttons and fields. Example: The 'Edit' button will be configured as: Visible only when s_status_group = OPEN_GROUP. Example: The 'Assign Team' button will be: Visible only when s_status_group = OPEN_GROUP and Role = Manager. Without the groups defined now, the Vienable configuration in Session 7 cannot be done. Part E — Updating the UI to Reflect Entity Configuration​ Now that d_complaints has Relations, Object Types, Status values, and an ID Series configured, the p_complaints page must be updated to expose and use these configurations. In this part you will: Add Relation-based TransNodes to p_complaints for d_complaint_item, d_complaint_voices, and d_complaints_attachment. Connect the s_complaint_item grid (already in the pa_comp_details tab from Session 2) to the d_complaint_item relation TransNode. Verify the complaint_id field auto-populates from the ID Series. Verify the s_status field on the search section and the detail form is bound and showing the correct status values. 📘 Why the UI Needs to Be Updated When you added Relations in Part A, the platform can now automatically fetch child records. But the Page Builder still needs to be told WHICH TransNode to use to access that relation data. A Relation-type TransNode in the Page Data Model references the relation name (pr_complaint_item) and automatically joins child records to the active parent complaint record. The complaint_id field in the form section can now be set to read-only since the ID Series will fill it — the user should not manually enter a complaint ID. E.1 — Add Relation TransNodes to the Page Data Model​ # Action Detail 1 Open Page Builder Navigate to Design Studio → Page Builder. Select customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the Edit icon to enable edit mode. 2 Select p_complaints Click p_complaints in the tree. Open the Page Data Model panel (right-side tab). 3 Review existing TransNodes You should see: search (Query), list (EntitySet / Transfer&Link from search), detail (Entity / Transfer&Link from list). These were created in Session 2. 4 Add complaint item TransNode Click the detail transnode → click + icon available next to r_complaint_item in unused properties. Fill: Path: complaint_items 6 Repeat Repeat Action 4 for relation voices, attachments 7 Save Click Save. E.2 — Wire the s_complaint_item Section to the Relation TransNode​ Need to create a s_complaint_item, s_complaint_voices, s_complaint_attachments section with screen_type as grid and bind with respective transnode. # Action Detail 1 Create s_complaint_item Right-click pa_complaint_details → new → section → right click section → rename : s_complaint_item 3 Mark type as section Add type = section for s_complaint_items layout 2 Open Detail panel Click s_complaint_item to open its Detail properties on the right. And fil title = items 3 Set TransNode path In the TransNode/Path field, set: complaint_items. This references the relation TransNode created in E.1 Step 4. 4 Add controls Right-click s_complaint_item → New → Controls. Add: item_id, product, issue_observed. Or drag from Page Data Model → d_complaint_item → Unused Properties. 5 Set screen type Confirm s_complaint_item screenType = grid. Set showTitle = true so the tab label 'Complaint Items' is visible. 6 Add Section Toolbar Right click on s_complaint_item → New → Toolbar Add and Delete buttons will be added to section if not enable showAdd and showDelete properties as true 7 Add Save Button Right click on the section toolbar → Action/Items → update text → add press event and select save from vh. 8 Add config Right click- s_complaint_item → new → config Add visibleRowCountMode = Fixed Repeat the same for s_complaint_voices and s_complaint_attachments as well with respective transnodes. E.4 — Verify s_status in Search and Detail Sections​ The s_status field is a system property. Now that Status values are configured in the BOL Editor (Part C), the status dropdown in the search section and detail form will automatically render the configured values (OPEN, INPROCESS, ON_HOLD, RESOLVED, CLOSED, REOPEN). # Action Detail 1 Click Show Full Preview Add the property in s_search and s_complaint_detail and In the Page Builder, click Show Full Preview to load live data. 2 Verify s_status in search bar In the search filter bar, click the Status dropdown. Verify the 6 status values appear: OPEN, INPROCESS, ON_HOLD, RESOLVED, CLOSED, REOPEN. 3 Click a complaint row Select any complaint record from the list. The detail area loads. 4 Verify complaint_id 1. For creating complaints with object_type enable showAddWithObjectType option for s_complaint_list section toolbar. 2. The complaint_id field should show the P-00001 or M-0001 format based on object_type (or different if the test record was created before the ID Series was set up — create a new record to confirm). 5 Verify Complaint Items tab Click the Complaint Items tab in the pa_comp_details area. If the selected complaint has items, they should appear in the grid. The tab was empty in Session 2 — it should now have a data source.

Naming Convention Summary​ Item Convention Example Primary Relation pr_<child_entity_short> pr_complaint_item Non-Primary Relation r_<entity_short> r_customer Object Group Lowercase, descriptive complaint_types Object Type UPPERCASE_WITH_UNDERSCORES PRODUCT_ISSUE Status Value UPPERCASE INPROCESS Status Group UPPERCASE_GROUP OPEN_GROUP ID Series ID id_<entity_short> id_complaint ID Prefix Uppercase abbreviation + dash CMP- Documentation Sources​ Topic Reference Relations — Create Relations BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 3.0.1 Create Relations Object Type & Group BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 3.0.1 Create Object Type and Object Group Status Configuration BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 3.0.1 Create Status and Status Group ID Series BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 3.0.1 Creating ID Series TransNode — Relation Type UI Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section on Page Data Model / TransNode configuration Jira — Relation field in Developer AI PROC-26283 (Developer AI: Delta Prompting for Relation, Status, Object Type) Jira — Relation entity search PROC-25430 (Playwright automation — relation entity dialog search) | Session 4 — Value Helps & Queries Duration: Full day | Pre-requisite: Session 3 assignment verified | | :---- |

Session Objectives​ By the end of this session, you will be able to: Understand the three types of Value Helps (VH Config, VH Query, VH Transaction) and when to use each. Create a VH Config for priority (Low / Medium / High / Critical) and nature_of_complaint, complaint_type fields. Create VH Query types that fetch data from d_customers and d_resp_team entities as picker suggestions. Understand what a KloQuery is and how it differs from a Runtime Entity query. Create two Saved Queries for the complaint list: My Complaints (filtered by assigned_to = current user) and All Open Complaints (filtered by s_status = OPEN). Assign Value Helps to entity properties in the BOL Editor. Update the UI — wire VH pickers and query-driven TransNodes into the p_complaints search and detail sections. 📘 What This Session Builds On Session 3 configured Relations, Object Types, Status, and ID Series on d_complaints — the structural foundation. Session 4 makes the user experience intelligent: instead of typing raw IDs, users get dropdowns and pickers. priority, complaint_type, nature_of_complaint → VH Config (fixed, app-managed lists). customer_id, responsible_team → VH Query (dynamic, fetched from d_customers / d_resp_team). Saved Queries → drive the different list views per role (My Complaints for Employee, All Open for Manager). Part A — Understanding Value Helps​ A.1 — What Is a Value Help?​ A Value Help (VH) is a platform-level component that provides a controlled list of choices for an entity property. When a VH is assigned to a property, the corresponding input field in the UI automatically renders as a dropdown (ComboBox), auto-complete field, or picker dialog (F4) — without any additional coding. The VH also validates that the entered value exists in the list when 'Is Restricted' is enabled. 📘 Three VH Types in Klobase (VH User Guide — Section 1.1) VH Config: Values are maintained in the metadata (config) DB. App-managed, flavor-dependent. Can be overridden by child apps. Requires a build after creation/update. Use for fixed classification lists (priority, complaint_type, etc.). VH Query: Values are fetched from a transactional or modelled query at runtime. Use for dynamic master data pickers (customer_id, responsible_team). The query determines what data appears in the picker. VH Transaction (DEPRECATED): Older type. Internally still supported for legacy apps. New development should use VH Config or VH Query instead. VH Type Source Naming Use Case for This App VH Config Metadata / Config DB vhc_<name> priority, complaint_type, nature_of_complaint VH Query Transactional / Modelled Query vhq_<name> customer_id → d_customers, responsible_team → d_resp_team A.2 — Value Helps to Create in This Session​ VH ID Type Property to Assign Description vhc_priority VH Config priority Low / Medium / High / Very High vhc_complaint_type VH Config complaint_type Software vhc_nature_of_complaint VH Config nature_of_complaint Hardware : Battery not charging vhq_customer VH Query customer_id Fetches from d_customers — key: customer_id, display: customer_name vhq_resp_team VH Query responsible_team Fetches from d_resp_team — key: emp_id, display: name Part B — Creating VH Config Value Helps​ B.1 — What Is VH Config and When to Use It?​ VH Config stores its values in the metadata database — the same database that stores entity definitions, page structures, and app metadata. These values are part of the application definition itself, not the transaction data. Use VH Config for lists that are defined once by the developer and rarely change: priority levels, complaint categories, nature classifications. B.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating vhc_priority​ Follow these steps to create the priority VH Config. Repeat the process for vhc_complaint_type and vhc_nature. # Action Detail 1 Open Data Studio Navigate to Design Studio → Data Studio. Select your application customer_complaints_<prid> from the dropdown. 2 Click + → Value Help Select entity. Click the Add icon (+) in the toolbar. A menu appears — select Value Help. The Value Help creation dialog opens. 3 Fill VH ID and Type Value Help ID: vhc_priority 5 Fill VH detail fields Description: Priority levels for customer complaints 6 Add VH Config items Click the Add (+) icon in the VH Config Items section. Add Row 1: Key: LOW 7 Save Click Save. vhc_priority is saved. Note: a build is required for this to appear in the UI — proceed to create all VH Configs first, then the trainer will trigger the build. B.3 — Assign VH Config to Entity Properties​ After creating all three VH Configs, assign each to the corresponding property in d_complaints. This is done in the Properties tab of the entity. # Action Detail 1 Select d_complaints In the Data Studio tree, click d_complaints. 2 Go to Properties tab Click the Properties tab. Locate the priority property row. 3 Set Value Help for priority Click the Value Help column cell for the priority row. A value help picker opens — type vhc_priority and select it. The VH ID is now assigned to the property. 5 Repeat for complaint_type and nature_of_complaint Assign vhc_complaint_type to complaint_type property. Assign vhc_nature to nature_of_complaint property. 6 Save Click Save. All three properties now have VH Config assignments. ✔ VH Config Checkpoint vhc_priority created — 4 items: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL. vhc_complaint_type created — 5 items matching the Object Types from Session 3. vhc_nature created — 4 items: TECHNICAL, LOGISTICS, COMMERCIAL, GENERAL. All 3 VH Configs assigned to their respective d_complaints properties. Save confirmed for all. Part C — Creating VH Query Value Helps​ C.1 — What Is VH Query?​ A VH Query fetches its suggestion items from a live entity or modelled query at runtime. Unlike VH Config (which is static metadata), VH Query shows records that are currently in the transactional database. This is the right choice for master entity pickers — where the data comes from d_customers, d_resp_team, or any other entity that can be searched and selected. 📘 VH Query Fields (BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 2.2.3 Value Help Detail) Entity/Query: The entity name or modelled query ID that returns the list of suggestions. Key Property: The property whose value gets STORED in the parent entity when the user selects an item. For d_customers → customer_id. Display Text: The property shown to the user in the dropdown/picker. For d_customers → customer_name. Desc Format: How the display appears. Example: :customer_id--:customer_name shows ID followed by Name. Icon: Optional — entity property that holds an icon URL to show alongside each suggestion item. C.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating vhq_customer​ # Action Detail 1 Click + → Value Help Select entity and In the Data Studio toolbar, click + → Value Help. Value Help ID: vhq_customer 2 Open vhq_customer Click vhq_customer in the tree. The Detail panel shows the VH Query configuration fields. 3 Set Entity/Query In the Entity/Query field, select d_customers. This means the VH will execute a runtime query against d_customers to fetch suggestion rows. 4 Set Key Property Key Property: customer_id. This is the value that gets written into d_complaints.customer_id when the user picks a customer. 5 Set Display Text Display Text: customer_name. This is what the user sees in the dropdown list. 6 Set Desc Format Desc Format: :customer_id--:customer_name. This renders as 'CUST-001 -- Acme Corp' in the picker field once a value is selected. 7 Save Click Save. vhq_customer is ready. Perform the same for vhq\_res\_team C.4 — Assign VH Query to Entity Properties​ # Action Detail 1 Select d_complaints → Properties tab Click on d_complaints in the tree and go to Properties. 2 Assign vhq_customer to customer_id Click the Value Help cell for customer_id. Select vhq_customer from the picker. Optionally mark Is Restricted = true to enforce that only valid customer records can be entered. 3 Assign vhq_resp_team to responsible_team Click the Value Help cell for responsible_team. Select vhq_resp_team. 4 Save Click Save. 💡 VH Type in the UI Control (KloControls 7.0 User Guide — KloInput) After assigning a VH to a property, the KloInput control in the UI renders differently based on the vhType setting in the Page Data Model or the control's properties panel. F4: Shows a full picker dialog when the user clicks the input — best for large datasets (d_customers with many records). ComboBox: Shows a dropdown list — best for small fixed lists (priority, complaint_type). AutoComplete: Shows suggestions as the user types — best for name-search scenarios. The platform automatically uses the appropriate type based on the VH type. You can override it in the Page Data Model or the control properties. Part D — Understanding and Creating KloQueries​ D.1 — What Is a KloQuery?​ A KloQuery is the Klobase equivalent of a SQL SELECT statement. It lets you define — within the Data Studio — exactly what records to fetch, from which entity, with which filters, joins, and sort order. Unlike a Runtime Entity Query (which simply fetches all records of an entity), a Modelled Query gives you full control over the WHERE clause, JOIN entities, and sort order — and is reusable across multiple pages. Query Type When to Use Runtime Query (Entity Query) Fetch all records of a single entity. No WHERE clause in the definition. Filters applied at runtime via the TransNode. Use for simple list screens. Modelled Query (Dynamic Query) Define custom WHERE conditions, joins, sort order in the BOL Editor. Reusable, entity-independent. Use for role-filtered lists (My Complaints), VH Queries backed by joins, aggregated results. Native Query (Advanced Query) Raw SQL. Database-specific. Use only for special cases not achievable with modelled queries. Avoid training. 📘 KloQuery Fields Reference (BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Section 3.0.2) Return Entity: The entity whose properties appear in the result set. Query Type: Runtime Entities And Join: Add the root entity and any joined entities (LEFT JOIN, INNER JOIN, etc.). Select Properties: Choose which properties from the entities appear in the result. Parameters: Define input parameters the query accepts at runtime (e.g., user_id filter passed from the TransNode). Where: Define filter conditions: entity.property = :parameter or entity.property = 'fixed_value'. Sort Order: Set the default sorting column and direction (ASC / DESC). Naming convention: Query IDs must start with q_. All lowercase. D.2 — Queries to Create in This Session​ Query ID Type Purpose q_complaints Modelled Employee: shows only complaints assigned to the logged-in user D.3 — Step-by-Step: Creating q_my_complaints​ # Action Detail 1 Click + → Query Select d_complaints entity and click + → Query. Fill : q_complaints and click create then save. 2 Open q_complaints Click q_my_complaints in the tree. The Detail panel shows the query configuration tabs. 4 Select Properties tab Click the Select Properties tab. By default, all d_complaints properties are included. Remove any you do not need to reduce payload. Keep it all for now. 5 Add Parameter Click the Parameters tab. Click Add. Parameter ID: current_user 6 Add WHERE clause Click the Where tab. Click Add. Fill: Entity Property: d_complaints.assigned_to 7 Add Sort Order Click the Sort Order tab. Click Add. Field: d_complaints.created_on 8 Save Click Save. q_my_complaints is ready. Part E — Saved Queries​ E.1 — What Is a Saved Query?​ A Saved Query is a named combination of a base query and a specific set of pre-filled search parameters. Where a Modelled Query defines the structure, a Saved Query defines a pre-configured instance of that query — ready to execute with one click in the search bar. Saved Queries appear as quick-filter options in the search TransNode of the UI. 📘 Saved Query vs Modelled Query (Basic Training Guide — Section 2.1) Modelled Query: The definition — entity, properties, parameters, WHERE logic. Reusable structure. Saved Query: A named configuration of a modelled query with preset parameter values. Stored per entity. In the UI, a Saved Query appears as a quick-filter button or dropdown in the search bar section. Saved Queries are created from the Data Browser (Advanced Search), not directly in the query detail tab. Naming convention for Saved Query IDs: Begin with sq_ by convention. E.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating a Saved Query from Data Browser​ # Action Detail 1 Open Data Browser Select d_complaints in the Data Studio tree. Click the data browser in the toolbar. The Data Browser opens. 2 Open Advanced Search In the Data Browser toolbar, click the Advance Search button. A search configuration dialog opens. 3 Select Base Query In the Query field of the Advance click + 4 Set parameter values Select customer_id in the left input and like in the middle input. Enter: $SYSTEM.userID as the parameter value. This means the saved query will always use the logged-in user's ID at runtime. 5 Save as Saved Query Click the Save Query button (or the Save icon in the Advance Search toolbar). Enter Saved Query ID: sq_my_complaints 6 Verify Click search. The Data Browser should show only complaints where assigned_to matches the current user (or empty if no matches). The saved query is now available. Part F — Updating the UI to Use Value Helps and Queries​ With all Value Helps and Queries configured in the BOL Editor, the p_complaints page now needs to be updated to use them. In this part you will: Update the search TransNode to use q_complaints_list as its data source. Add the quick-filter Saved Query buttons (sq_my_complaints, sq_all_open) to the search section. Verify that priority, complaint_type, customer_id, and responsible_team fields in the form render as dropdowns/pickers automatically. Set the vhType on customer_id and responsible_team controls to F4 (full picker dialog). F.1 — Update the TransNode to Use q_complaints_list instead d_complaints​ Currently the search TransNode uses the default entity fetch. Switching it to q_complaints_list gives you control over sort order and allows future WHERE customisation. # Action Detail 1 Open Page Builder Navigate to Design Studio → Page Builder. By the end of this session, you will be able to: Set up the Private Node development environment and understand the TypeScript entity file structure. Understand the entity lifecycle and all hook methods: onAfterCreate, OnValidate, onDelete. Write and test server-side default value logic: auto-set s_status = OPEN and assigned_to = current user on complaint creation. Implement property-level Getter and Setter overrides to compute derived fields (actual_tat, full customer display). Write business rule validations in OnValidate: mandatory field checks, date constraints, role-based restriction. Implement query-level beforeQ / afterQ callbacks: enforce row-level, role-based visibility before a query runs, and reshape/compute values across the result set after it returns. Apply the landing page concept: prepare the p_complaints page to function as the application's primary home screen post-login. 📘 What This Session Builds On Sessions 1–4 built the data model, page structure, VH pickers, and queries — all through the low-code tools (Data Studio, Page Builder). Session 5 crosses the threshold into code: you will write TypeScript in the entity .ts file, running server-side in the Klobase Node.js runtime. The entity file is the ONLY place business logic belongs. Never write business rules in the controller file. Session 5 follows the core platform principle: Business logic → Entity file. UI orchestration → Controller file. Reference: PROC-23582 (Validation Logic to Be Maintained in Entity Callback onValidate Methods instead of Controller files). Part A — Setting Up the Private Node Environment​ Reference: Private Node setup Guide The Private Node is a local Node.js server running on your laptop that acts as the workspace server for your development session. Instead of your browser talking to the shared landscape server, it talks to your VS Code instance — giving you full debugging capability and instant iteration on server-side code. Pre-requisites​ Requirement How to verify VS Code installed Open VS Code — if it opens, you are good. Procify VSIX extension installed Extensions (Ctrl+Shift+X) → search 'Procifynow'. If not installed, ask the trainer for the VSIX file. Network access to the landscape Open your landscape URL in a browser. If the login page loads, connectivity is confirmed. Node.js installed Open a terminal: node --version. You should see v22+. Setting the Private Node in VS Code​ 1 Create Your Workspace Folder Create a new folder on your laptop: Documents/PrivateNode/srm_<your_prid>. All application server-side files will be downloaded here. 2 Open the Folder in VS Code File > Open Folder > navigate to your new folder > click Open. 3 Open the Command Palette Press Ctrl+Shift+P (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+Shift+P (Mac). 4 Run Procify Version Selection Type: Procifynow: Procify IDE Setup and press Enter. A WebView panel opens on the right. 5 Enter Your Landscape URL In the WebView, enter your app URL — e.g. https://dev.procify38.com/p6/srm_pr0045/index.html. Click Next. 6 Enter Developer Credentials Enter your developer username and password. Click Start Setup. 7 Wait for Initialisation The VS Code file explorer will populate with folders (entity stubs, controller stubs, kloconfig, etc.). A confirmation message appears when complete. 8 Checkout application The VS Code will open a webview to checkout the assigned apps. Select the created app and perform checkout A.2 — Entity File Location and Structure​ The entity .ts file for d_complaints is located in the Private Node workspace at the path: workspace/apps/<your_app_id>/d_complaints.ts If the file does not exist yet, the private node can generate it. The base structure looks like this: import { KloEntity, ValidationError, ErrorType } from 'klobase'; export class d_complaints extends KloEntity { // ── Getters & Setters ────────────────────────────────────────── // ── Lifecycle Hooks ──────────────────────────────────────────── public async onAfterCreate(): Promise<any> { // Called after a new complaint record is created } public async OnValidate(): Promise<any> { // Called during navigation if transnode setActiveIf = Valid } public async onDelete(): Promise<any> { // Called after the record is deleted } } 💡 Architecture Principle: Business Logic Belongs Here The entity file is the authoritative location for all business logic. Period. Controller file → UI orchestration only (navigation, formatter functions, show/hide decisions). Entity file → field defaults, cross-field computations, validations, role enforcement. Never duplicate validation logic in the controller. If the controller calls commitP(), OnValidate() fires automatically on the server — that is your safety net. Reference: kloTouch 7.0 Basic Training Guide — Section 7.5 Best Practice Do's and Don'ts (Entity File). Part B — Entity Lifecycle Hooks​ B.1 — The Three Hook Methods​ Klobase provides three entity lifecycle hook methods that you override in the entity .ts file. These run on the server and are triggered automatically by the platform at the appropriate point in the entity's lifecycle. Method When Called Trigger Condition Primary Use onAfterCreate() After entity is created in DB On every new entity save Set defaults, auto-populate audit fields, initialise related records OnValidate() During navigation / on save / validateP function TransNode setActiveIf = 'Valid' Validate field values, enforce business rules, push errors onDelete() After entity is deleted On every delete operation Cascade cleanup, logging, send notifications 📘 OnValidate — Important Details OnValidate is triggered ONLY when the TransNode's 'setActiveIf' property is set to 'Valid' in the Page Builder. If setActiveIf is not set, OnValidate does NOT fire — the platform skips validation on navigation. Inside OnValidate, push errors using: this.errors.push(new ValidationError(this, propertyId, errorCode, message, ErrorType.ERROR)); The method must NOT return the errors array — it pushes to this.errors and the platform reads it. (PROC-24075 fixed this for proper return type.) ErrorType.ERROR blocks save. ErrorType.WARNING allows save but shows a warning toast. After your OnValidate runs, the platform ALSO runs its own mandatory-field validation based on key attributes — you don't need to repeat those. B.2 — Configuring TransNode setActiveIf for Validation​ Before OnValidate can fire, the TransNode that holds the complaint detail must be configured with setActiveIf = Valid in the Page Builder. # Action Detail / Code 1 Open Page Builder Navigate to Design Studio → Page Builder. Select customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the Edit icon. 2 Select the detail TransNode Click p_complaints in the tree. Open the Page Data Model panel. Click on the 'detail' TransNode row. 3 Set setActiveIf = Valid In the TransNode detail section (right side), find the 'setActiveIf' property. Change from the default (Always) to 'Valid'. This means: when the user tries to navigate away from the detail form, the platform will call OnValidate first. If errors exist, navigation is blocked. 4 Save Click Save. Part C — Entity Rules​ C.1 — What are Entity Rules?​ Rules contain business logic codes. It works with the event bus, any change in the entity will trigger the event, and all the rules hooked with the event will be executed sequentially. Rules are reusable objects across client, server and middleware. EX: When a complaint is created by an employee then status should be OPEN and assigned_to should be the same user. A responsible team/manager/assigned_to can be assigned by the manager only. An employee or manager can delete the complaint but not the responsible team Field Default Value Logic s_status 'OPEN' — every new complaint starts in OPEN status assigned_to this.txn.getUserID() — auto-set to the logged-in user who created the complaint created_on this.s_created_on — already auto-set by system field, no action needed created_by this.s_created_by — already auto-set by system field, no action needed C.2 — How to create an Entity Rule?​ Step 1: Go to the Rule tab and click on the add icon(+). Field Description Event type Select the event type. Based on the type of event you choose, the rule will be executed. Type Select the channel type, based on this the transaction will be performed. Exit ID is an ID you put in for the rule subscription. (can select from the existing one). Clazz This will be the rule file name. Invocation Method The method needs to be called. Step 2: Select the Event Type from the drop-down. The event type will mention when the rules will be executed. Event types: On Create ( rule will be executed on create of an entity) On Delete (rule will be executed on delete of an entity) On Update (rule will be executed on update of an entity) Rest of the types will be covered in future. Step 3: Select the channel type(there are different input channels to perform a transaction on an entity, channel type selection decides when to trigger the Rule). Channel Type: Endpoint / Device on Klarion server- always on the client Endpoint / Device on Klarion server Endpoint / Device on Klarion server- always on server(current focus) Endpoint / Device to Server/ Client -Network Context Switch Legacy on Klarion server Klarion server to Klarion offline server Klarion server to Klarion Server Step 4: Fill in the value for Exit ID. Exit ID: It's an ID that you put in for the rule subscription. (can select from the existing one). Step 5: In the Clazz field provide the rule file name (example: rules/<file_name>) and in the invocation method provide an event name. You will be using that event to write your business logic codes. NOTE: If you are creating a Rule for the same entity you can fill this inside the Clazz field. Step 6: Click on the save button to save the newly created rule. C.3 — Implementing onCreateRule for default values​ As mentioned above, create a rule for onCreate with channel type as ALWAYS_ON_SERVER with class as this. Create Entity Folder and d_complaints.ts file | public async onCreateComplaint(oEvent:any): Promise<any> { // Auto-set status to OPEN on every new complaint let complaint = oEvent.getObject(); complaint.s_status = 'OPEN'; // Auto-set assigned_to to the creating user's login ID const currentUser = this.txn.getUserID(); complaint.assigned_to = currentUser; // Log for debugging (visible in Private Node terminal) this.info('Complaint created by:', currentUser, '| Status set to OPEN'); } | | :---- | 📘 this.txn — The Transaction Object (BOL API Reference) Inside entity hooks, oEvent.getTxn() gives you access to the KloTransaction object — the server-side context for the current request. oEvent.getTxn().getUserID() → returns the login ID of the user who triggered the save. Use for audit fields. oEvent.getTxn().getValueBag() → a key-value store local to the current transaction. Good for passing data between hooks. this.info(), this.warn(), this.error() → server-side logging methods. Output appears in the Private Node terminal and the Google Cloud logs. C.4 — Testing onCreate​ # Action Detail / Code 1 Typescript compilation Run tsc -w in one terminal 2 Save d_complaints.ts In VS Code, save the file. The Private Node auto-reloads — watch the terminal for 'server restarted' or similar message. 3 Create a new complaint in the UI Open the browser, navigate to p_complaints. Click the Add button in the section_toolbar of the detail area. The new record form opens. 4 Fill minimal fields and save Enter complaint_desc: 'Test Create logic'. Select priority = HIGH. Click Save (commitP from the Save button). 5 Verify in Data Browser Open Data Studio → d_complaints → Test → Data Browser. The latest record should show: s_status = OPEN, assigned_to = your login ID (e.g. PR0045). C.5 — Implementing onUpdate for assignee​ As mentioned above, create a rule for onUpdate with channel type as ALWAYS_ON_SERVER with class as this. Create Entity Folder and d_complaints.ts file if not available public async onUpdateComplaint (oEvent:any): Promise<any> { // Auto-set status to OPEN on every new complaint Let complaint = oEvent.getObject(); Const = previousState = await complaint.fromP() if((previousState.assigned_to != complaint.assigned_to)&& oEvent.getTxn().$SYSTEM.roleID != ‘EMPLOYEE_MANAGER’){ Throw Error (‘team assignment should be done by manager’)//Make “T” in to a //lowercase } } C.6 — Implementing onDelete for validation​ As mentioned above, create a rule for onUpdate with channel type as ALWAYS_ON_SERVER with class as this. Create Entity Folder and d_complaints.ts file if not available public async onDeleteComplaint (oEvent:any): Promise<any> { if(oEvent.getTxn().$SYSTEM.roleID == ‘IT_TEAM’){//Change ’ ’ to “ ”this Throw Error (‘it_team cannot delete complaint’)//Make “T” in to a lowercase } } ​ Part D — Property Setters and Getters​ D.1 — What Are Setters and Getters?​ TypeScript property accessors let you intercept reads and writes of entity properties. In Klobase, setters and getters in the entity .ts file are the correct place for computed/derived field logic — not the controller. Pattern Purpose Setter (set propertyId) Called every time the property value changes. Use to: compute a derived field when an input changes, enforce value formatting, trigger side-effects. Getter (get propertyId) Called every time the property value is read. Use to: return a computed / formatted value instead of the raw stored value. ⚠ Critical Setter Pattern — Always Call this.s() Inside a setter, you MUST call this.s('propertyId', new_value, 'dataType', false, false) to actually persist the new value into the entity's internal state. Without this.s(), the new_value is accepted by TypeScript but never written to the entity data — the save will ignore your change. Pattern: if(new_value == this.propertyId) return; // guard to avoid infinite loop Then: this.s('propertyId', new_value, 'dataType', false, false); D.2 — Setter: Auto-Compute actual_tat When closed_on Changes​ When a complaint is closed (closed_on is set), actual_tat should be computed as: (closed_on - created_on) in days. public set closed_on(new_value: Date) { if (new_value == this.closed_on) return; this.s('closed_on', new_value, 'date', false, false); // Compute actual_tat when closed_on is set if (new_value && this.s_created_on) { const msPerDay = 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24; const diffMs = new Date(new_value).getTime() - new Date(this.s_created_on).getTime(); this.actual_tat = parseFloat((diffMs / msPerDay).toFixed(1)); } } D.3 — Getter: Display complaint_id with Priority Badge​ A getter can return a formatted composite string. For example, a display_title getter that combines complaint_id and priority: // t_ prefix = transient property (not stored in DB) // Define t_display_title as a Transient property in the BOL Editor first public get t_display_title(): string { return `${this.complaint_id} [${this.priority || 'UNSET'}]`; } 📘 Transient Properties (BOL Editor 7.0 User Guide — Entity Property Qualifier) Transient properties (t_ prefix) are computed at runtime and NOT stored in the database. They must still be defined as entity properties in the BOL Editor with qualifier = Transient. Once defined, they can be added to sections and controls in the Page Builder like any other property. The getter in the .ts file provides the value — the platform reads the getter whenever the control renders. Use transient properties for: display labels, formatted dates, computed totals, role-based display logic. Part E — Writing Business Rule Validations in OnValidate​ E.1 — Validation Rules for the Customer Complaints App​ Based on the BRD from Session 1, the following validations must be enforced when a complaint is saved: Rule ID Field(s) Condition Message V001 complaint_desc Empty or length < 10 chars Complaint description must be at least 10 characters. V002 priority Empty (null or blank) Priority is required. Please select Low / Medium / High / Critical. V003 planned_resolution_date Set AND is before today's date The planned resolution date cannot be in the past. V004 planned_resolution_date Set AND is before created_on The planned resolution date cannot be before the complaint creation date. V005 s_status Attempt to set CLOSED but role is Employee Employees cannot close a complaint. Only the manager can close. E.2 — Implementing OnValidate​ | public async OnValidate(): Promise<any> { // V001 — complaint_desc minimum length if (!this.complaint_desc || this.complaint_desc.trim().length < 10) { this.errors.push(new ValidationError( this, 'complaint_desc', 'V001', 'Complaint description must be at least 10 characters.', ErrorType.ERROR )); } // V002 — priority is required if (!this.priority) { this.errors.push(new ValidationError( this, 'priority', 'V002', 'Priority is required.', ErrorType.ERROR )); } // V003 — planned_resolution_date not in the past if (this.planned_resolution_date) { const today = new Date(); today.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0); if (new Date(this.planned_resolution_date) < today) { this.errors.push(new ValidationError( this, 'planned_resolution_date', 'V003', 'Planned resolution date cannot be in the past.', ErrorType.ERROR )); } } // V004 — planned_resolution_date not before created_on if (this.planned_resolution_date && this.s_created_on) { if (new Date(this.planned_resolution_date) < new Date(this.s_created_on)) { this.errors.push(new ValidationError( this, 'planned_resolution_date', 'V004', 'Planned resolution date cannot be before the complaint creation date.', ErrorType.ERROR )); } } } | | :---- | 📘 Role Rollup Values (Training Guide Beginner — Session 1 Part A) s_role_rollup is the numeric role hierarchy value assigned to application roles. Owner (Employee role) → s_role_rollup = 10 Supervisor (Manager role) → s_role_rollup = 20 Reviewer (ResponsibleTeam role) → s_role_rollup = 30 Lower number = higher priority. Manager (20) overrides Employee (10). You can also use this.txn.hasPermission('permission_id') for custom permission checks. See Permissions User Guide. E.4 — Testing OnValidate​ # Action Detail / Code 1 Save d_complaints.ts Save the file. Private Node restarts automatically. 2 Test V001 — short description In the UI, open a complaint detail. Clear the complaint_desc field or enter only 3 characters. Click Save. The platform should block navigation and highlight complaint_desc with the error message 'Complaint description must be at least 10 characters'. 3 Test V002 — missing priority Clear the priority field. Click Save. Priority field should be highlighted with the V002 error message. 4 Test V003 — past date Set planned_resolution_date to yesterday. Click Save. Should show V003 error on the date field. 5 Test V005 — Employee closing complaint Log in as emp_<prid> (Employee role). Open a complaint. Change s_status to CLOSED. Try to Save. Should see V005 error. Log in as mgr_<prid> (Manager) — same operation should succeed. 6 Verify valid record saves Fill all required fields correctly with a future resolution date. Click Save. Record should commit without errors. Check Private Node terminal — no error logs. Part E — Query Rules E.1 — What are Query Rules? `Query rules are similar to Entity rules but are triggered before and after a query execution rather than around a create/update/delete. They are the correct place to answer two very different questions: Before the database is asked anything — “what should this user even be allowed to see?” (row-level filtering, defaulting search criteria). After the database has answered — “does the raw result need reshaping before it reaches the client?” (adding computed fields, merging data from a second query, masking sensitive values, sorting/aggregating in ways the query modeller can’t express. Both callbacks receive an EventContext (commonly named oEvent) and give access to the query instance itself via oEvent.getObject(). E.1 — How to Create Query Rules? Creating query rules is the same as creating entity rules, except the event type you subscribe to is one of: Event types: Before Query (beforeQ) — executes before the query is fired against the database. Anything set on the query object here becomes part of the WHERE condition. After Query (afterQ) — executes after results come back from the database, before they are returned to the client. The raw result set can be read and replaced here. Query Rule Event Reference (BOL API) Event.getObject() — returns the KloQueryForRule instance being executed. Set properties on it to add filter conditions (beforeQ), or call getResults() / setResults() on it to read/replace the raw result rows (afterQ). Event.getTxn() — returns the KloTransaction for the current user; use it to read $SYSTEM.roleID, call this.txn.get$User(), or check permissions. Event.getEventType() — returns which event fired, e.g. BEFORE_QUERY or AFTER_QUERY. Useful if one method is wired to handle both events. queryInstance.getResults() / setResults() — read or replace the raw JSON array of result rows in an afterQ callback. These are plain objects, not KloEntity instances — they cannot be saved back. E.3 — Implementing before Query on q_complaints​ As we already know from the BRD document complaints page behaviour will be different based on role. In case of employee only complaints raised by him should be visible In case of manager all the complaints should be visible In case of it_team only assigned tickets should be visible Create query folder and q_complaints.ts public async beforeQ(oEvent: EventContext) { let obj : any = oEvent.getObject(); let role = oEvent.getTxn().$SYSTEM.roleID; if(role === 'EMPLOYEE'){ obj.customer_id = (await this.txn.get$User()).login_id; obj.s_created_by = (await this.txn.get$User()).login_id; // Added for Business AI }else if( role == "IT_TEAM"){ obj.assigned_to = (await this.txn.get$User()).login_id; } if(obj.description) { obj.description = `%${obj.description}%`; } } E.3 — validate before query implementation​ Validate both the screen and data browser that data should be filtered based on role. E.4 — Testing beforeQ​ # Action Detail / Code 1 Save q_complaints.ts Private Node restarts automatically. 2 Test as Employee Log in as emp_<prid>. Open the complaints list screen. Only complaints where customer_id equals this employee’s login ID should appear, even though no filter was set from the UI. 3 Test as Manager Log in as mgr_<prid>. The full, unfiltered list should be visible — confirming the if block only narrows the query for EMPLOYEE and IT_TEAM roles. 4 Test as IT Team Log in as it_team_<prid>. Only complaints where assigned_to equals this user should appear. 5 Test in Data Browser Repeat the same three logins in the Data Browser (not just the app screen) against q_complaints. The same role-based filtering must hold — beforeQ applies at the query level, so it protects every entry point, not just one screen. Part E.1 — Implementing after Query on q_complaints​ Scenario​ The Manager’s complaint list needs a column showing how many days a complaint has been open — days_open — without storing it on the entity (it changes every day, so persisting it would immediately go stale). This is a textbook afterQ use case: compute it once, on the way out, from data already in the result set.​ Implementing afterQ​ public async afterQ(oEvent: EventContext) { let queryInstance = oEvent.getObject(); let results = await queryInstance.getResults(); let today = new Date(); let newResults = results.map((row: any) => { if (row.s_created_on) { let created = new Date(row.s_created_on); let diffMs = today.getTime() - created.getTime(); row.days_open = Math.floor(diffMs / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24)); } else { row.days_open = 0; } return row; }); queryInstance.setResults(newResults); } ​ ​ Wiring days_open into the UI​ Add days_open as a transient property (Session 5, Part D) on d_complaints so the Page Builder can bind a column to it, then add that column to s_complaints (Session 2, Part B.9.2). Because the value arrives already computed on the result row, no additional binding logic is needed on the client.​ Testing afterQ​ # Action Detail / Code 1 Save q_complaints.ts Confirm no errors in the Private Node terminal on restart. 2 Open the complaints list as Manager The new days_open column should show a whole number for every row. 3 Create a fresh complaint Its days_open should read 0 on the day it is created. 4 Cross-check one row against Data Browser Compare s_created_on for that record against today’s date manually — the displayed days_open should match. ​ Part F — Preparing the Landing Page​ F.1 — What Is a Landing Page?​ The landing page is the first screen a user sees after logging into the application. In the Customer Complaints Application, p_complaints_dash will serve as the landing page — the list of complaints filtered by role will be immediately visible after login. There are two things needed to make p_complaints_dash the effective landing page: Create a dashboard screen. Configure it as landing page The screen we are going to create will be as mentioned below. F.1 — create dashboard screen?​ Dashboard also follows p_complaints page with limited changes # Action Detail / Code 1 Create dashboard page Navigate to the page builder screen and select customer_complaints application. And create a blank page. Add items aggregation 3. Expand and right click on items:<control-id> new → control → m.Text → text: New 4.
