Session Objectives​ By the end of this session, you will be able to: Understand and apply all four binding modes in Klobase: Value, Path, Parts (with formatter), and Expression. Write expression bindings for visibility, enabled state, and dynamic text. Write and wire formatter functions in the controller. Implement all navigation scenarios using navTo: section nav, page nav, key-based nav, query-param nav. Apply pre-defined and user-defined style classes to controls, sections, page areas, and layouts. Part A — Data Bindings In Depth​ Every control on a Klobase screen reads and writes data through the Transaction Model ($M). The model is a JSON model object. All bindings use the prefix $M to reference it. Without a binding, a control shows a static value or nothing at all — it is disconnected from the live data. A.1 — The $M Model Path Structure​ The Transaction Model is organized as a tree. Each TransNode in the Page Data Model corresponds to a branch in the $M tree. The full path to any property follows this pattern: {$M>/transNodeRelationId/propertyId} For a list TransNode with relationId = list, the first row's complaint_desc is: {\$M\>/list/0/complaint\_desc} For the detail TransNode with relationId = detail: {\$M\>/detail/complaint\_desc} The leading / after > is mandatory. Omitting it causes a silent bind failure. A.2 — The Four Binding Modes​ Mode When to Use Syntax / Where to Set Example Value Static, hardcoded value — no model connection. Control always shows this literal text regardless of data. Properties tab → Value field text = 'Complaint ID' — always shows that label. Path Bind to exactly ONE model property. Two-way binding by default: changes in UI write back to model. Properties tab → DSRC field {$M>/detail/complaint_desc} — shows and edits the complaint description. Parts Combine MULTIPLE paths into one display value via a formatter function. Always one-way (read only). Properties tab → dsrc field (add each path as a part) + Formatter Function field Parts: {$M>/detail/first_name} + {$M>/detail/last_name} → formatter returns full name string. Expression Inline calculated value. No formatter function needed. Supports ternary operators and comparisons. Always one-way. Properties tab → dsrc field (starts with {= ...}) {= ${$M>/detail/is_escalated} === true ? 'Escalated' : 'Normal'} ⚠ Path and Parts are mutually exclusive on the same property — you cannot use both at once. If you need multiple values combined, always use Parts. A.3 — Path Binding: Step-by-Step​ Path binding wires one control property to one model property. This is the most common binding type for form fields. # Action Detail 1 Select the control in the tree Example: select the complaint_desc m.Input control inside s_complaint_details section. 2 Open Properties tab Detail panel (right side) → Properties tab. 4 Enter the binding in dsrc Type: {$M>/detail/complaint_desc} — the detail TransNode relationId followed by the property ID. 5 Save and verify in Full Preview The field loads with the active complaint's description. Edit it and save — the new value persists in the database. 📘 The TransNode relationId is set in the Page Data Model, not the entity name. If your detail TransNode's relationId is complaints_detail, the path is {$M>/complaints_detail/complaint_desc}. A.4 — Parts Binding with Formatter Function​ Use Parts when you need to combine or transform multiple model values into a single display string. Parts binding is one-way only — it cannot write back to the model. Value:​ The value field will hold the value provided for the property. Path:​ In this path field, users can only bind with exactly one property or value. This can be used if there is only one property to bind. Parts:​ In this path field, users can bind multiple properties or values. This can be used if multiple values or properties need to be provided for binding. (Note: If we are using formatter function, then it is mandatory to provide either parts or path value) Formatter Functions​ Controller function name (formatter function) can be given for the field. Type:​ In the type field, the user can provide the datatype for the control’s value. Formatter Options:​ Formatter options define how a value is formatted and displayed in the UI. Validation Constraint:​ Constraints are optional and define how an input value that is entered in the UI should look like. During parsing, the value is validated against these constraints. For example, an Integer type has a constraint for the maximum that is automatically validated when parsing the input values. Example: displaying TAT status as a composite string from actual_tat and standard_tat. // Controller function — formatTAT public formatTAT(actual: number, standard: number): string { if (!actual || !standard) return '—'; const diff = actual - standard; if (diff <= 0) return `✅ On Time (${actual} days)`; return `⚠ Overdue by ${diff} day(s) — Actual: ${actual}, SLA: ${standard}`; } ⚠ The formatter function receives Part values in the exact order they appear in the Parts list. If you add actual_tat first and standard_tat second, the function signature must be formatTAT(actual, standard). Part B — Expression Bindings​ Expression binding lets you write a JavaScript ternary expression directly inside a binding path string. It starts with {= and ends with }. It is evaluated live at runtime whenever the bound model values change. B.1 — Syntax Rules​ Rule Detail Starts with {= The expression must begin with {= (curly brace, equals). Without the =, it is treated as a plain path, not an expression. Reference model paths with ${} Inside an expression, wrap every $M path in ${}: ${$M>/detail/s_status}. This dereferences the path to its current value. Must return a value The expression must evaluate to a value matching the property type. visible expects boolean. text expects string. enabled expects boolean. Ternary only for simple cases Use condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse. Complex multi-branch logic belongs in a formatter function, not in expression binding. No function calls You cannot call controller functions from expression binding. Use Parts + formatter for that. B.2 — Expression Binding Examples (Customer Complaints App)​ Use Case Property Expression Explanation Show Save/Cancel only in EDIT or CREATE mode visible {= ${$M>/TransactionMode } === 'EDIT' Make Edit button invisible in EDIT mode visible {= ${$M>/TransactionMode } === 'DISPLAY' ? true : false} Edit button should disappear the moment the user clicks it and mode switches to EDIT. Show escalation badge only when escalated visible {= ${$M>/detail/is_escalated} === true ? true : false} is_escalated is a Boolean property. Bind to the is_escalated path directly. Dynamic text: 'Escalated' vs empty text {= ${$M>/detail/is_escalated} === true ? 'ESCALATED' : ''} Shows ESCALATED label text conditionally. Returns empty string otherwise. Disable complaint_desc when not OPEN enabled {= ${$M>/detail/s_status} === 'OPEN' ? true : false} The complaint description should only be editable when the complaint is in OPEN status. Dynamic placeholder label for priority text {= ${$M>/detail/priority} === 'VERY_HIGH' ? '🚨 Critical' : ${$M>/detail/priority}} Shows emoji label for critical priority, falls back to raw value for others. TAT warning color class {= ${$M>/detail/actual_tat} > ${$M>/detail/standard_tat} ? 'tat-overdue' : 'tat-ok'} Applies different CSS class depending on whether actual exceeds standard TAT. ⚠ Expression binding is evaluated once per model change event. For heavy computation (e.g. comparing arrays or doing date math), use a formatter function instead — expression binding performance degrades with complex logic. Part C — Formatter Functions​ A formatter function is a TypeScript method in the controller file that takes one or more raw model values as input and returns a formatted display value. It is the right tool whenever expression binding would become too long, needs multi-step logic, or needs to look up external data. C.1 — Where Formatter Functions Live​ Formatter functions are public methods on the controller class. They must be public — the framework calls them reflectively from the Page Builder binding. export class p_complaints extends KloController { // Formatter functions — called from Parts binding in Page Builder public formatPriority(priority: string): string { const map: Record<string,string> = { 'LOW': '🟢 Low', 'MEDIUM': '🟡 Medium', 'HIGH': '🔴 High', 'VERY_HIGH': '🚨 Very High' }; return map[priority] || priority || '—'; } } C.2 — Formatter Function Examples for the Complaints App​ Function Name Input Parts Return Example Output formatPriority(priority) {$M>/detail/priority} string 🔴 High formatTAT(actual, standard) {$M>/detail/actual_tat}, {$M>/detail/standard_tat} string ⚠ Overdue by 3 day(s) formatStatusLabel(status) {$M>/detail/s_status} string 🟠 IN PROCESS formatFullName(first, last) {$M>/detail/created_by_first}, {$M>/detail/created_by_last} string John Doe formatEscalationText(isEsc, type) {$M>/detail/is_escalated}, {$M>/detail/complaint_type} string ESCALATED — BILLING formatDateAge(createdOn) {$M>/detail/created_on} string 3 days ago C.3 — Wiring a Formatter Function: Complete Steps​ # Action Detail 1 Write the function in controller.ts Open the controller file in Online Code Editor. Add a public method with the formatter logic. Ensure it takes the exact number of parameters as the number of Parts you will add. 2 Select the target control Page Builder → select the control whose display property you want to format (e.g. m.Text for priority display). 3 Delete existing Path binding If a Path binding exists on the property, clear it first — Parts and Path cannot coexist. 4 Switch to Parts Properties tab → click Parts radio button. 5 Add each Part in order Click + for each model path. Order matters: Part 1 = first function argument, Part 2 = second argument, etc. 6 Set Formatter Function field Type the exact function name as it appears in the controller. No parentheses, no 'this.' prefix. 7 Private Node must be running Formatter function calls go to the running Private Node. Start your Private Node before testing. Without it, the binding silently returns undefined. 8 Save and Full Preview The control should now render formatted output. Open Chrome DevTools Sources to debug if the output is wrong. ⚠ Formatter functions must be PURE — they should not modify model state, call APIs, or have side effects. They are called repeatedly on every model refresh. Side effects cause unpredictable behavior and performance issues. Part D — Navigation In Depth​ Navigation in Klobase is handled exclusively through the navTo() controller API. All legacy navigation methods (navToS, navToByEvent, navToScreenByKeyScreen) are deprecated — always use navTo. It is defined on KloController and is available in every page controller via this.navTo(). D.1 — navTo Parameter Reference​ Parameter Type Purpose Example SS string Navigate to a section (PageArea or Section) WITHIN the same page. Used for list-to-detail navigation on the same screen. SS: 'pa_complaint_details' S string Navigate to a DIFFERENT page by page ID. S: 'p_customers' D string Navigate to a page AND set a specific record as active by its primary key. Format: entity@@key@@suffix. D: 'd_complaints@@CMP-00012@@F' QP object Navigate to a page AND apply a query parameter filter on the target page's search TransNode. QP: { complaint_type: 'BILLING' } F string Navigate to a specific flavor (application variant). F: 'flavor_prod' Mode string Set the page mode on the target page when navigating. Values: DISPLAY, EDIT, CREATE. Mode: 'CREATE' AppData object Pass arbitrary data to the target page. Read from controller using this.getAppData(). AppData: { source: 'dashboard' } D.2 — Navigation Scenarios with Code​ Scenario 1 — List row click navigates to detail section on the same page: // Press event on ticket_id m.Link control: await this.navTo({ SS: 'pa_complaint_details' }, oEvent); // oEvent is required for SS nav — it carries the row index for setActive Scenario 2 — Navigate to a different page: await this.navTo({ S: 'p_customers' }); Scenario 3 — Navigate to a different page AND a specific section within it: await this.navTo({ S: 'p_customers', SS: 'pa_customer_details' }, oEvent); Scenario 4 — Navigate to a page and load a specific record by key (requires navbykey on target TransNode): const key = this.tm.getTN('list').getProperty(`${idx}/complaint_id`); await this.navTo({ S: 'p_complaints', SS: 'pa_complaint_details', D: `d_complaints@@${key}@@F` }); // Target page's detail TransNode must have navbykey: {"sourcePath": "list"} Scenario 5 — Navigate and pre-filter with query parameters (requires navbyquery on target TransNode): const type = this.tm.getTN('detail').getProperty('complaint_type'); await this.navTo({ S: 'p_complaints', SS: 'pa_complaints', QP: { complaint_type: type } }); // Target page's search TransNode must have navbyquery: {"sourcePath": "search"} Scenario 6 — Navigate to Create mode on a different page: await this.navTo({ S: 'p_complaints', Mode: 'CREATE' }); D.3 — navbykey and navbyquery Configuration​ Config Field Where to Set Value Format When Required navbykey Target page's detail/list TransNode → Properties → navbykey field {"sourcePath": "list"} — the list TransNode relationId of the TARGET page Required when using D: parameter in navTo. It tells the target page which TransNode to activate. navbyquery Target page's search TransNode → Properties → navbyquery field {"sourcePath": "search"} — the search TransNode relationId of the TARGET page Required when using QP: parameter in navTo. It tells the target page to filter using the passed query params. Part E — Style Classes for Controls, Sections, Page Areas & Layouts​ The Style Classes tab in the Page Builder is the single place to control all visual formatting. It has two modes: QuickAdd (pre-built bundles) and Manual (full control). Different QuickAdd bundles are available depending on what is selected in the tree: a Section, a PageArea/PageLayout, or a Control. E.1 — QuickAdd for Sections​ QuickAdd Style Applied On What It Does When to Use Card Sections (form/detail type) Adds a white background, rounded corners, drop shadow, and inner padding. Renders the section as a card floating above the page. Detail form sections (s_detail_header, s_complaint_details). Makes key information stand out. Grid Sections (grid type) Adds alternating row colors, column borders, header background, and hover highlight. Improves readability for dense tabular data. List sections (s_complaints). Always apply Grid QuickAdd to any grid-type section. Transparent Sections Removes background and border. Content sits directly on the page background. Dashboard tile sections where background should show through. E.2 — QuickAdd for Controls​ QuickAdd Style Applied On What It Does Font Size (S/M/L/XL) m.Text, m.Label, m.Input Applies a pre-defined font size class. Use L for emphasis, S for secondary information in grid cells. Text Colour Any text control Applies a branded color from the platform color palette. Includes: primary (blue), success (green), warning (orange), danger (red). Bold m.Text, m.Label Applies font-weight: bold. Use for headers, primary identifiers (complaint_id), and totals. Italic m.Text Applies font-style: italic. Use for secondary metadata (timestamps, remarks). Background Color Any control Applies a background highlight. Useful for dashboard tiles and key metrics. Color Combination Any control Pre-defined foreground + background pairs ensuring WCAG contrast compliance. Safer than picking colors individually. E.3 — Format Rules (Conditional Styling)​ Format Rules apply a style class conditionally based on the control's current value. This is how status badge colors work. Configure via Style Classes tab → Category + Style Class + Format Rule + Format Value. Field What It Does Example Category What CSS property the rule affects: Background, Text, or Icon. Background Style Class The CSS class name to apply when the condition is true. status-open Format Rule The condition type: Text Contains, Text Equals, Text Starts With, etc. Text Contains Format Value The value of the control's text must match for the class to apply. OPEN Full Row When checked, the style applies to the entire grid row instead of just the cell. Checked for critical priority rows that need full-row coloring. Status badge rules for the complaints app — apply to s_status control in both s_complaints grid and s_detail_header: Status Value Category Style Class Format Rule Format Value OPEN Background status-open Text Contains OPEN REOPEN Background status-reopen Text Contains REOPEN INPROCESS Background status-inprocess Text Contains INPROCESS ON_HOLD Background status-onhold Text Contains ON_HOLD RESOLVED Background status-resolved Text Contains RESOLVED CLOSED Background status-completed Text Contains CLOSED E.4 — User-Defined CSS Classes​ When QuickAdd and Format Rules are not sufficient, create custom CSS classes in the Settings Editor. # Action Detail 1 category Select category as user defined 2 Style class Provide your own style class 3 Add css file Maintain css file in css folder 4 Load file in controller FileLoaderUtils.loadCSSFile(this.getFlavor(), this.getFlavorVersion(), "myStyleSheet"); "myStyleSheet" this is the style sheet has been created CSS Usage — Do's & Don'ts​ ✓ Do​ Recommendation ✓ ✓ Use Style Classes first. Use Category + Style Class + Format Rule (Quick Add ) before creating a custom CSS file(user defined). ✓ ✓ Scope custom CSS to the flavor. Wrap CSS rules in .procify__<app_id> { ... }, using the flavor name without the version. ✓ ✓ Load CSS in onpageInit(). Use FileLoaderUtils.loadCSSFile(this.getFlavor(), this.getFlavorVersion(), "myStyleSheet");. ✓ ✓ Use SAPUI5/OpenUI5 classes. Target classes such as .sapMIBar, .sapUiTableRow, .sapMTB, and .KloTabContainerHeaderToolbar. ✓ ✓ Test across supported platforms. Verify custom CSS on APK, IPA, Safari, and Chrome before releasing it. ✓ ✓ Use :has() for whole-grid-cell styling. Add a User Defined class to the control and use td:has(.yourClassName) { ... } when the entire cell must be styled. ✓ ✓ Check layout configuration first. For height, spacing, or positioning issues, check screenType options such as fit_to_area, hsplitter, vsplitter, and grid_layout before overriding CSS. ✓ ✓ Order Format Rules carefully. Place general rules first and more-specific rules later when values can overlap. ✗ Don’t​ Avoid ✗ ✗ Don’t use unsupported Format Rule types. Only Always, Text Contains, and Formula are supported. ✗ ✗ Don’t use overlapping Text Contains values without checking the order. For example, OPEN also matches REOPEN. ✗ ✗ Don’t expect CSS to inherit between flavors. A child flavor must load its own stylesheet. ✗ ✗ Don’t assume embedded screens inherit CSS. Each screen must load the CSS it requires. ✗ ✗ Don’t modify Shared flavor CSS without checking the current access policy. Confirm with the platform team before making changes. ✗ ✗ Don’t use Style Class alone to color an entire grid cell. It styles the control inside the cell, not the <td>. ✗ ✗ Don’t leave the Style Class field empty. An empty Style Class prevents the style from being applied. ✗ ✗ Don’t hardcode custom class names in multiple places. Once loaded, the class is available under Category: User Defined in the Style Class UI. Reuse that class instead. F — Implement binding in application​ As you might have already seen that we already used bindings to attach data to control. G — Implement styling​ As you can see the customer complaints showed and the one we are developing functionality might be looking the same at this point but ui is looking different which is due to styling difference. Let's implement styling. G.1 — list screen​ Add formatting to complaint_id to change it to bold. Add font color to s_status based on value Add font and background color for status in detail header Style all the form sections in pa_comp_details. Properties tab → Path field: {$M>/detail/prop} Expression binding Inline ternary for conditional visible/enabled. Path field: {= condition ? true : false} navTo (Events tab / press event) Navigates to a section or page on control interaction. Events tab → press → NavTo function Layout type = header Pins s_detail_header at top of pa_complaint_details. Detail panel → type = header Layout type = section Sets pa_comp_details as scrollable body area. Detail panel → type = section saveTransaction Controller function. Saves dirty data, triggers OnValidate, resets to DISPLAY. press event inline function refreshTransnode Controller function. Reverts unsaved changes, resets mode to DISPLAY. press event inline function Status Group badge Format Rule Text Contains using group-level IDs: OPEN, INPROCESS, ACCEPTED, COMPLETED. Style Classes tab → Format Rule Quick Add style Pre-defined style bundle for Grid or Card sections. Style Classes tab → QuickAdd

Session Objectives​ By the end of this session, you will be able to: Configure Vienable for all four dimensions: Screen Size, Page Mode, Role Rollup, and Status Group. Understand and correctly use all five controller page lifecycle hooks. Use the full TransNode and TransModel controller API set. Vienable (Visible + Enable) is the declarative system for controlling control visibility and editability across four independent dimensions. The final result for any control is the intersection of all configured dimensions: a control is visible only if ALL applicable dimension rules say it should be visible. A.1 — The Four Vienable Dimensions​ Dimension What It Controls Values Configuration Location Page Size Visibility/enable by device screen resolution. Evaluated based on the PARENT section's resolved size. S (phone), M (tablet), L (desktop), XL (wide desktop) Vienable Dashboard → Page Size columns: S, M, L, XL Page Mode Visibility/enable by current screen interaction mode. Default mode is DISPLAY. Display, Edit, Create, Review Vienable Dashboard → Page Mode columns Role Visibility/enable by the logged-in user's s_role_rollup value. Config must be maintained in BOL Editor → Object Type tab. Owner (10), Supervisor (20), Reviewer (30), Overlooker (40). In this app: EMPLOYEE=10, EMPLOYEE_MANAGER=20, IT_TEAM=30 Vienable Dashboard → Role column Status Group Visibility/enable by the bound entity's current s_status_group value. Config must be maintained in BOL Editor → Status tab. The Status Groups you defined in Session 3. In this app: OPEN, INPROCESS, ACCEPTED, COMPLETED Vienable Dashboard → Status Group column ⚠ Entity must be set to TRUE for the control row in the Vienable Dashboard. If Entity = false, Role and Status Group dimensions are ignored — the control will always be visible/enabled regardless of role or status. A.2 — Screen Size Vienable (Responsive Layout)​ Screen size Vienable controls which columns/fields appear on small vs large screens. This is how the platform supports mobile without a separate build. Page Size Approx. Viewport Recommended for Complaints App S Up to ~600px (phone) Show only: ticket_id (link), priority, s_status. Hide: complaint_desc, customer_id, dates, responsible_team. M 601–1024px (tablet) Show: ticket_id, priority, s_status, complaint_type. Still hide verbose date columns. L 1025–1440px (desktop) Show all columns. Standard desktop experience. XL Above 1440px (wide desktop) Same as L. Use for additional panel layout or expanded detail. Steps to configure phone layout for s_complaints grid: # Action Detail 1 Open Vienable Dashboard Page Builder → p_complaints page → Vienable tab → Vienable Dashboard sub-tab. 2 Set Entity = true for each grid column control Find complaint_desc, customer_id, first_response_date, responsible_team in the Control ID column. Toggle Entity to true. 3 Set S column = Hidden for verbose columns For each verbose column: click the S (phone) cell → set to Hidden (🚫 icon). 4 Keep S = Visible for essential columns ticket_id, priority, s_status: ensure S is set to Visible (👁 icon). 5 Test with Preview In → Phone Toolbar → Preview In → Phone. Grid should show only the essential 3 columns. 6 Verify desktop unaffected Preview In → Desktop. All columns must still show. A.3 — Page Mode Vienable​ Control Display Mode Edit Mode Create Mode Rationale Edit button Visible Hidden Hidden Edit disappears when clicked (mode switches to EDIT). Save button Hidden Visible Visible Only meaningful when there is something to save. Cancel button Hidden Visible Visible Only meaningful when there is something to discard. Delete button Visible Hidden Hidden Deletion is a display-mode action (select then delete). complaint_desc input Show As Label Depends on Role Editable Read-only in display, role-controlled in edit. responsible_team input Show As Label Depends on Role Editable for MANAGER only Only manager assigns team. A.4 — Role Rollup Vienable​ Role-based Vienable uses the s_role_rollup value of the logged-in user. This value is set in BOL Editor → Object Type tab → role configuration table (KloTuner config). The mapping for this is: Application Role Procify Role s_role_rollup Vienable Role ID Employee Owner 10 EMPLOYEE Manager Supervisor 20 EMPLOYEE_MANAGER Responsible Team Reviewer 30 IT_TEAM Role-based Vienable rules for p_complaints — key controls: Control EMPLOYEE EMPLOYEE_MANAGER IT_TEAM Delete button (toolbar) Hidden Visible (OPEN group only) Hidden responsible_team field (EDIT) Show As Label Editable Show As Label complaint_desc field (EDIT) Editable (OPEN group only) Show As Label Show As Label assigned_to field (EDIT) Show As Label Editable Show As Label remark field (EDIT) Hidden Editable Editable A.5 — Status Group Vienable​ Status Group maps a set of s_status values to a group name. The configuration is in BOL Editor → Status tab. Vienable evaluates the group of the entity's CURRENT s_status to decide visibility. Status Group Name Statuses It Covers Typical Vienable Use OPEN OPEN, REOPEN Edit button visible. complaint_desc editable for EMPLOYEE. INPROCESS INPROCESS, ON_HOLD Edit button visible. Assign team button available for MANAGER. ACCEPTED RESOLVED Edit button hidden — complaint resolved, no edits allowed. COMPLETED CLOSED Edit button hidden — complaint closed. Only the Reopen button is shown. ⚠ Status Group Vienable requires Entity = true on the control row AND the entity's Status tab must have the groups configured in BOL Editor. Missing group config causes the status group column to be ignored — the control remains visible regardless of status. A.6 — Apply vienability for application.​ s_complaint_details should not be editable in display mode Desc and priority should be editable for OPEN/REOPEN status only For closed complaints nothing should be editable. s_timeline_details Time line details should be editable in edit mode only. Timeline details should be editable by manager only. Actual tat should not be editable at any time. s_assigment_details Assignment details should be editable in both edit and create mode Assignment details should be editable by manager only S_admin_details Admin details should not be editable S_complaints_list should not be editable in display mode s_voices_list should not be editable in display mode S_attachment_list should not be editable in display mode

documents.t: The Klobase framework calls lifecycle hook methods on your controller class at specific points in the page's life. Understanding WHEN each fires is essential — using the wrong hook causes bugs that are hard to trace because they appear intermittently depending on navigation order. B.1 — Hook Execution Order​ On first page load: onPageInit → onPageModelReady → onPageEnter On forward navigation back to same page: onPageEnter (only) On backward navigation away from page: onPageExit (source page), onPageEnter (target page) On back-navigation that destroys the page: onPageExit → onPageDestroy B.2 — Lifecycle Hook Reference​ Hook When It Fires Model Data Available? Primary Use Cases Common Mistakes onPageInit Once, when controller class loads. UI, model, and TransNodes do NOT exist yet. No Rare: one-time non-model setup like subscribing to a global service. Trying to access this.tm or TransNodes — they are null at this point. onPageModelReady Once (per page lifecycle), after TransNodes are initialized but BEFORE data is fetched. No (TransNodes exist but have no data) Call this.tm.getTN('search').skipModelPreparation() to skip auto-query execution and manually control data load. Reading TransNode data — getData() returns null or empty. The fetch hasn't happened yet. onPageEnter Every time the page becomes visible — forward nav, backward nav, and initial load. Yes Dashboard count calculations. Resetting UI state. Refreshing summaries. Setting default filter values. Putting logic that should only run ONCE here — it re-runs on every navigation. Use _initialized flag for one-time logic. onPageExit When the user navigates AWAY to a different page. Yes Auto-save draft, log exit event, clear unsaved state. Not called for within-page section navigation (SS). Only fires on cross-page navigation. onPageDestroy Once, when the page is removed from memory (back-nav that exits the page history). Partially Unsubscribe event listeners. Release resources. Not needed for most standard screens. Using it as a reliable 'save on exit' hook — the page may be destroyed without user navigation (memory pressure, app backgrounding). B.3 — onPageEnter: The Most Important Hook​ onPageEnter is the page lifecycle hook. It fires with data already loaded, on every navigation — making it perfect for dashboard counts, summaries, and state resets. This event will be called whenever the screen enters the visible area by means of navigation (Both front and back navigation). public async onPageEnter(): Promise<void> { // ── 1. One-time initialization guard ────────────────────────────────── if (!this._initialized) { this.\_initialized \= true; // Logic that must run only ONCE goes here } // ── 2. Dashboard count computation (server-side aggregate) ──────────── // "status_count_query" = a query-type transnode configured with: // SELECT s_status, COUNT(k_ticket_id) AS count_of_status // FROM <entity> WHERE <same filters as before> GROUP BY s_status const countQueryTN = this.tm.getTN('status_count_query').getData(); const aggregateResult = await countQueryTN.executeP(); const rows = aggregateResult; const counts: Record<string, number> = { OPEN: 0, REOPEN: 0, INPROCESS: 0, ON\_HOLD: 0, RESOLVED: 0, CLOSED: 0 }; rows.forEach((row: any) => { const st \= row.s\_status || ''; const c \= Number(row.count\_of\_status) || 0; if (counts.hasOwnProperty(st)) counts\[st\] \= c; }); // Build the derived object once, then set it on a dedicated // "other"-type transnode used purely for binding — no full row payload involved. const statusCount = { t\_open\_count: counts.OPEN \+ counts.REOPEN, t\_inprocess\_count: counts.INPROCESS \+ counts.ON\_HOLD, t\_resolved\_count: counts.RESOLVED, t\_closed\_count: counts.CLOSED }; await this.tm.getTN('status_count').setData(statusCount); }

documents.t: C.1 — TransModel APIs (this.tm.*)​ API Signature Returns Description getTN() this.tm.getTN(relationId: string) TransNode Get a TransNode by its relationId (as configured in Page Data Model). The gateway to all TransNode operations. commitP() this.tm.commitP(success, failure, validate, isDisplayMode) Promise<any> Save all dirty objects in the Transaction Model to the database. validate=true triggers OnValidate. isDisplayMode=true resets to DISPLAY after save. rollBackTxn() this.tm.rollBackTxn() Promise<void> Revert ALL unsaved changes across all TransNodes back to last commit state. Used by Cancel button. getAllTransNodes() this.tm.getAllTransNodes() TransNode[] Get all TransNodes on the page. Useful for bulk operations. getTransactionFromTransnodeData() this.tm.getTransactionFromTransnodeData(tn) any Get the raw transaction object from a TransNode. Advanced use only. C.2 — TransNode APIs (this.tm.getTN('id').*)​ API Signature Returns Description & Example getData() .getData() KloEntitySet / KloEntity / KloQuery Get all data from the TransNode. For list TransNodes returns the full entity set. Call .toArray() on the result to iterate. data = this.tm.getTN('list').getData(); getActiveData() .getActiveData() KloEntity Get only the currently active (selected/highlighted) entity. data = this.tm.getTN('detail').getActiveData(); getProperty() .getProperty(path: string) any Get a single property value from the TransNode model. For list rows: getProperty('0/complaint_id') — index/propertyId format. For detail: getProperty('complaint_desc'). setProperty() .setProperty(path, value) TransNode Set a property value — triggers immediate UI re-render. For transient/display properties. setProperty('t_open_count', '5'). setData() .setData(val, index?) Promise<void> Set the entire dataset for a TransNode. Replaces current data. Used after manual data fetch. this.tm.getTN('list').setData(entitySet); setActive() .setActive(index) Promise<bool> Set the active row by index. Triggers onArrive and updates all child TransNodes. await this.tm.getTN('list').setActive(0); getActiveIndex() .getActiveIndex() number Get the current active row index. Useful before navigating away. idx = this.tm.getTN('list').getActiveIndex(); getSelectedEntities() .getSelectedEntities(ssID?) KloEntity[] Get all checked rows in a grid section (multi-select). selected = this.tm.getTN('list').getSelectedEntities(); executeP() .executeP() Promise<void> Re-execute the query associated with a query-type TransNode. Use to refresh data without full page reload. await this.tm.getTN('search').executeP(); applySortP() .applySortP(property, order) Promise<void> Sort the TransNode data by a property. order: 'ASCENDING' or 'DESCENDING'. await this.tm.getTN('list').applySortP('created_on', 'DESCENDING'); createEntityP() .createEntityP(json, successMsg, errorMsg) Promise<KloEntity> Create a new entity and add to the TransNode. Triggers onAfterCreate hook server-side. await this.tm.getTN('list').createEntityP({complaint_desc: 'test'}, 'Created', 'Failed'); C.3 — Controller Navigation & UI APIs​ API Signature Description navTo() await this.navTo(params, oEvent?) Navigate to section or page. See Part D of Session 6 for full parameter reference. setMode() this.setMode('EDIT' 'DISPLAY' saveTransaction() this.saveTransaction(successMsg, errorMsg, validate, resetMode) Commit dirty data, optionally trigger OnValidate, and optionally reset to DISPLAY. Standard Save button handler. refreshTransnode() this.refreshTransnode(nodeId, mode, discard) Refresh a named TransNode, set its mode, and optionally discard unsaved changes. Standard Cancel button handler. showBusy() this.showBusy(msg?, id?) Show the platform busy/loading indicator. Use during async operations. this.showBusy('Loading...'); hideBusy() this.hideBusy(id?) Hide the busy indicator. Always call in a finally block to ensure it's dismissed even on error. getAppData() this.getAppData() Retrieve AppData passed from the source page's navTo call. Returns the object passed as AppData: {...}. getPathFromEvent() this.getPathFromEvent(oEvent) Get the model path string from a press event. Use with getTN().getProperty(path.split('/')[2] + '/propertyId') to get a specific row value.

documents.t: Client-side validation in Klobase operates at two levels: (1) field-level required constraints using the 'required' property, and (2) full-form OnValidate triggered by commitP or saveTransaction. Both are enforced in the browser before any network call is made. D.1 — Required Field Validation​ Mark a control as required by adding the 'required' property and setting it to true. The platform renders a red asterisk and prevents submission if the field is empty. # Action Detail 1 Select the input control Page Builder → select the mandatory field control, e.g. complaint_desc m.Input. 2 Add 'required' property Properties tab → Add → required → set Value to true. 3 Test in Full Preview (CREATE mode) Click New → leave complaint_desc empty → click Save. Platform shows required validation error and blocks save. D.2 — OnValidate (Server-Side Validation Triggered from Client)​ OnValidate runs in the entity file (.ts) on the Private Node when saveTransaction is called with validate=true. The client sends the dirty object to the server; the server validates and returns errors if any rule fails. The client then displays these errors as message dialogs. // In d_complaints.ts entity file — OnValidate hook public async OnValidate(oEvent: IKloEvent): Promise<void> { const entity = oEvent.getEntity(); const errors: string[] = []; // V001: Description must be at least 20 characters if (!entity.complaint_desc || entity.complaint_desc.length < 20) { errors.push('V001: Complaint description must be at least 20 characters.'); } // V002: Priority is mandatory if (!entity.priority) { errors.push('V002: Priority is mandatory.'); } // V003: Cannot close without a remark if (entity.s_status === 'CLOSED' && !entity.remark) { errors.push('V003: Remark is required when closing a complaint.'); } if (errors.length > 0) { oEvent.setError(errors.join('\\n')); } } For OnValidate to fire from the UI, the detail TransNode's setActiveIf must be set to 'Valid' in the Page Data Model. Without this, saveTransaction with validate=true does nothing. # Action Detail 1 Set setActiveIf on detail TransNode Page Data Model → click detail TransNode → setActiveIf dropdown → select Valid. 2 Call saveTransaction with validate=true Edit button press: this.setMode('EDIT'). Save button press: this.saveTransaction('Saved.', 'Save failed.', true, true). 3 Test validation Leave complaint_desc with fewer than 20 characters → Save → OnValidate fires → error message dialog shows V001 text. 4 Fix and retry Enter a valid description → Save → passes validation → data persists → mode resets to DISPLAY.

These standards are non-negotiable on all Procify projects. Violations result in code review rejection and technical debt. The principles come from kloTouch 7.0 Basic Training Guide §7.4 and §7.5. E.1 — Controller File Standards​ Rule Do Don't Reason Scope Write ONLY UI logic in the controller: formatters, navigation, show/hide, model reads for display. Write business logic (status transitions, validations, default-setting) in the controller. Business logic in the controller bypasses server validation and breaks when the screen is accessed via API. TypeScript typing Declare every variable with its type: const count: number = 0; const msg: string = ''; Use implicit any: let x = someValue; or omit types on function parameters. Untyped code hides bugs at compile time that surface as runtime errors in production. Variable declaration Declare variables only when necessary. Prefer const over let. Declare variables at file scope (class properties) when a local variable suffices. File-scope variables persist across page navigations and cause state leakage between sessions. Nested functions Keep functions flat. Extract complex logic to named private methods. Nest arrow functions inside controller methods: onClick(() => { const x = () => {...}; }) Nested functions are not testable, not readable, and difficult to debug. Async/await Use async/await for all TransNode API calls. Mark the function async. Use .then().catch() promise chains. Consistent await pattern is required by the framework for proper error propagation. Deprecated APIs Always use navTo(), tm.commitP(), this.setMode(). Use navToS(), navToByEvent(), getTN('x').commitP() Deprecated APIs are removed in future versions. Using them creates upgrade risk. Model mutation Only modify model properties via setProperty() for transient display values. Directly mutate entity properties from the controller (entity.some_prop = value). Direct mutations bypass the dirty-tracking mechanism and do not persist on save. E.2 — Entity File Standards​ Rule Do Don't Scope Write ONLY business logic in entity files: onCreate defaults, onUpdate role checks, onDelete restrictions, beforeQ filtering, OnValidate. Write navigation or UI state changes in entity files. Setter functions Use setter override pattern to automatically derive related values when a property changes. Compute derived values in the controller on button press — this is bypassed when data changes via API. Validation location All mandatory field checks and business rule violations go in OnValidate. Throw errors in onAfterCreate — onAfterCreate is called AFTER the record is saved; errors there cause data inconsistency. Error handling Always wrap async BOL API calls (createEntityP, LoadEntityByKeyP) in try/catch and log errors. Let unhandled promise rejections propagate silently. Role checks in rules Use oEvent.getTxn().$SYSTEM.roleID to get the runtime role and enforce role-specific logic. Hardcode user IDs or email addresses for role checks. E.3 — Naming Conventions​ Item Convention Example Pages p_ prefix + snake_case description p_complaints, p_complaint_dashboard Page Areas pa_ prefix pa_complaint_details, pa_complaints Sections s_ prefix s_complaints, s_detail_header Entities d_ prefix d_complaints, d_complaint_item Queries q_ prefix q_complaints, q_customers Transient properties t_ prefix t_open_count, t_selected_count Controller functions (formatters) format + PascalCase formatPriority, formatTAT, formatStatusLabel Controller functions (event handlers) on + PascalCase + action onEditPress, onSavePress, onDeleteConfirm Variables in TypeScript camelCase + explicit type const openCount: number = 0; Boolean variables is/has prefix isEscalated, hasAttachment, isLoading ⚠ Private Node must be running whenever you test controller functions, formatter functions, or OnValidate. Without the Private Node, server-side hooks are bypassed and the client shows incorrect results. Always verify Private Node status in the Dev Tools toolbar before testing.

Concept What It Does Where Controller TypeScript UI orchestration only: formatters, model reads/writes for display, dashboard counts. workspace/apps/<app>/p_complaints.controller.ts TransNode setProperty() Updates a model property — triggers UI re-render immediately. Controller function body Vienable — Role Visibility by role ID: EMPLOYEE, EMPLOYEE_MANAGER, IT_TEAM. Vienable Dashboard → Role column Vienable — Status Group Visibility by status group: OPEN, INPROCESS, ACCEPTED, COMPLETED. Vienable Dashboard → Status Group column Vienable — Page Mode Visibility by DISPLAY/EDIT/CREATE. Vienable Dashboard → Page Mode columns $SYSTEM.roleID Runtime role ID of the logged-in user. Used in Entity/Query Rules for role checks. oEvent.getTxn().$SYSTEM.roleID in rules onPageEnter Controller hook fires after page data loads. Use for dashboard count calculations. p_complaint_dashboard.controller.ts

documents.t: ⚠ Complete ALL mandatory tasks before Session 8 Session 8 finalises the menu, home page, versioning, and publishing — the application must be fully working. Mandatory Tasks​ # Action Detail 1 Verify formatPriority formatter Full Preview: complaint with priority = VERY_HIGH shows '🚨 Very High — Immediate Action'. All 4 priority values formatted correctly. 2 Verify Vienable — Edit button CLOSED complaint (COMPLETED group): Edit button absent. OPEN complaint (DISPLAY mode): Edit visible → click → disappears. 3 Verify complaint_desc by role emp_<prid>: OPEN complaint → Edit → complaint_desc editable. INPROCESS complaint → Edit → complaint_desc is Show As Label. mgr_<prid>: always Show As Label. 4 Verify responsible_team by role emp_<prid> in EDIT mode: responsible_team is Show As Label (cannot assign). mgr_<prid> in EDIT mode: responsible_team is editable. 5 Verify dashboard counts p_complaint_dashboard shows live counts. Create/close complaints and reload — counts update correctly. 6 Verify screen size Vienable Page Builder Preview In → Phone: grid shows only ticket_id, priority, s_status. Desktop: all columns visible. | Session 8— App Management, Versioning & Publishing Duration: Full day | Pre-requisite: Session 8 assignment verified | | :---- |

Session Objectives​ By the end of this session, you will be able to: # Objective 1 Create the application menu using the Menu Editor — matching the BRD menu structure exactly. 2 Configure the HomePage Editor to add screen tiles for all three personas. 3 Understand the App Status Lifecycle: ACTIVE → RELEASED → DEPRECATED, and when to transition. 4 Create an App Branch from an RELEASED version and understand the branch-to-version merge workflow. 5 Run Validate & Publish — identify and fix blockers before triggering a Full Build. 6 Transport the published application from DEV to QA using the Transport tool. 7 Perform an end-to-end smoke test covering all three personas (Employee, Manager, IT Team). ⚠ Important Pre-requisite Check — Trainer will verify ALL of these before Session 8 begins. ✔ p_complaints page is fully built: search, list, detail with all tabs populated. ✔ Status badges (OPEN/INPROCESS/etc.) are rendered with correct colours. ✔ Vienable is configured: Edit/Save/Cancel button visibility by Role, Mode, and Status Group. ✔ Dashboard (p_complaint_dashboard) is set as Landing Page for all three roles. ✔ formatPriority formatter renders priority with emoji labels. ✔ OnValidate blocks V001–V005 violations correctly. ✔ All three test users (emp_<prid>, mgr_<prid>, it_<prid>) can log in and see the application. If any item above is incomplete, resolve it BEFORE starting Session 8. 📘 Reference / Tip BRD Quick Reference for Session 8 (from Session 1 Part A) Menu structure: ONE item — 'Complaints' → p_complaints Icon: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Roles: ALL Pages defined in BRD: p_home_page (home screen tiles) and p_complaints (main screen). p_complaint_dashboard = Landing Page (Session 5) — auto-loads on login. Does NOT need a menu entry. App ID format: customer_complaints_<your_prid> e.g. customer_complaints_pr0045

documents.t: A.1 — What Is the Menu Editor?​ The Menu Editor (also called Menu Builder per PROC-26419) is the tool you use to define the navigation structure visible to users in the hamburger menu of the application at runtime. Without a menu entry, users cannot navigate between screens — they would need to know URLs manually. Access path: Running app → Hamburger menu (☰) → Dev Tools → Menu Editor. A.2 — Menu Fields Reference​ Field Description Rules / Notes Menu ID Unique identifier for this menu item. ONLY alphanumeric + underscores. NO hyphens ( - ). NO spaces. Case-sensitive. Wrong: mn-complaints. Correct: mn_complaints. Target Page Page ID the menu item navigates to. Use the Value Help (VH) icon to pick from existing pages. Do NOT type the page ID manually. Menu Text Label shown to the user in the hamburger menu. Keep it short. Title case. Localisation supported. Page Parameters Optional JSON for navTo params (SS, QP, D, Mode). Leave blank for simple page nav. Not needed for the Complaints entry. Menu Icon SAP icon URI displayed alongside the text. Format: sap-icon://<icon-name>. Must be a valid SAP UI5 icon name. Example: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts. Sequence Sort order in the menu. Lower number = appears first. Use multiples of 10 (10, 20, 30) to leave room for future items. Roles Restrict visibility to specific application roles. Leave BLANK = visible to ALL roles. Fill role IDs (comma-separated) to restrict. Test Navigation Validates the menu item navigates correctly. Always click Test Navigation before saving — catches target page errors early. A.3 — BRD Menu Structure to Implement​ Menu Field Value Menu ID mn_complaints Target Page p_complaints (select from VH) Menu Text Complaints Menu Icon sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Sequence 10 Roles Leave blank — visible to ALL roles (Employee, Manager, IT Team) Page Parameters Not required — leave blank A.4 — Step-by-Step: Creating the Application Menu​ 1 Open Menu Editor In the running application, open the hamburger menu (☰ top-left). Go to Dev Tools → Menu Editor. 2 Select the Application In the App dropdown at the top of the Menu Editor, select customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the Edit button (pencil icon ✏). The menu table becomes editable. 3 Add a Header Group Click Add (+) → Add Header. Fill in: Menu ID: hdr_main Menu Text: Main Sequence: 10 Roles: leave blank Click OK. (A Header groups child items visually in the menu.) 4 Add the Complaints Child Menu Item Select the hdr_main row in the table. Click Add (+) → Add Child. Fill in: Menu ID: mn_complaints Target Page: p_complaints (use VH picker) Menu Text: Complaints Menu Icon: sap-icon://customer-and-contacts Sequence: 10 Roles: leave blank Click OK. 5 Test the Navigation Click Test Navigation on the mn_complaints row. p_complaints should open correctly. If a 'Page not found' error appears — check that the Target Page is exactly p_complaints (no typos). 6 Save Click the Save button (disk icon 💾). Wait for the busy dialog to close. A success toast confirms the menu is saved. 7 Verify with All Personas Log out and log in separately as emp_<prid>, mgr_<prid>, and it_<prid>. In each session, open the hamburger menu. The 'Complaints' item must be visible and navigate to p_complaints for ALL three test users. ⚠ Important Common Menu Editor Mistakes Hyphen in Menu ID: mn-complaints causes the item to save but NEVER appear in the app. Always use underscore: mn_complaints. Typing Target Page manually: Always use the VH picker. Manual typos cause silent navigation failures. Saving without testing: Always click 'Test Navigation' before saving. It catches missing pages early. Role restriction accident: If the menu item is set to a specific role, other personas cannot see it. Leave Roles blank for all-role visibility.

B.1 — What Is the HomePage Editor?​ The HomePage Editor configures which screen tiles appear on the application's built-in Home grid — accessible via the Home (🏠) icon. This is separate from the Landing Page (p_complaint_dashboard configured in Session 5). The Landing Page loads automatically on login. The Home grid gives users tile-based navigation to frequently used screens. 📘 Reference / Tip Three 'home' concepts — don't confuse them Landing Page (Session 5): Configured via Landing Page Settings. Auto-loads after login. Shows p_complaint_dashboard. HomePage Editor: Tile grid shown when user clicks the Home (🏠) icon. Configure p_complaints and p_complaint_dashboard tiles here. p_home_page (BRD): A screen defined in the BRD. Can be built as an additional home screen — not required for this session's delivery. B.2 — HomePage Editor Fields Reference​ Field Description HomePageID Unique ID for this tile. Convention: hp_<screen_short_name>. Screen The Page ID this tile navigates to. Use VH to select. Position Where the tile appears on the home grid. Use 'Body' for standard tiles. Sequence Order of the tile. Lower = appears first. Role Restrict tile visibility to specific roles. Leave blank = all roles. B.3 — Step-by-Step: Adding Tiles to HomePage Editor​ 1 Open HomePage Editor Hamburger menu (☰) → Dev Tools → HomePage Editor. Select customer_complaints_<prid> from the App dropdown. Click the Edit icon (✏). 2 Add the Dashboard Tile Click Add (+). HomePageID: hp_dashboard Screen: p_complaint_dashboard (select via VH) Position: Body Sequence: 5 Role: leave blank (all roles) Click Save (do NOT navigate away yet). 3 Add the Complaints Tile Click Add (+). HomePageID: hp_all_complaints Screen: p_complaints (select via VH) Position: Body Sequence: 10 Role: leave blank (all roles) Click Save. 4 Save All Click the Save icon (💾) in the toolbar. Wait for busy dialog to close. Success toast confirms. 5 Verify Log out. Log in as emp_<prid>. Click the Home (🏠) icon. Two tiles must appear: 'Dashboard' and 'Complaints'. Click each tile — verify it navigates to the correct screen. Repeat with mgr_<prid> and it_<prid>.

C.1 — App Status Values​ Every version of an application on the Procify platform has a Status that controls what operations are allowed on it. Understanding these statuses is essential before releasing or transporting. Status Meaning Can Develop? Can Transport? Can Create New Version? ACTIVE Current working version. All development happens here. ✅ Yes ❌ No ❌ No RELEASED Development complete and locked. Ready for transport. ❌ No ✅ Yes ✅ Yes (create from RELEASED) DEPRECATED Retired. Superseded by a newer version. ❌ No ❌ No ❌ No DISCARDED Abandoned branch/version. Excluded from main path. ❌ No ❌ No ❌ No ⚠ Important Critical Versioning Rules — memorise these before proceeding A NEW VERSION can only be created from a RELEASED version. A BRANCH can only be created from an ACTIVE version. Branch flavors CANNOT be transported. Merge the branch into a new version first, then transport. Once status is changed to RELEASED, no further development is possible on that version. Always build (Validate & Publish) BEFORE changing status to RELEASED. C.2 — Step-by-Step: Releasing the Application​ 1 Navigate to Account Console (also called Workspace Hub) Open the hamburger menu → Sys Admin → Account Console (or Workspace Hub). Alternatively: Hamburger menu → My Apps (if visible in your role). 2 Find Your Application In the Apps list, search for customer_complaints_<prid>. Click the App ID to open the application detail screen. 3 Open Edit Mode Click the Edit button (pencil icon ✏) in the toolbar. The Status field becomes editable. 4 Change Status to RELEASED In the Status dropdown, select RELEASED. Read the confirmation message carefully — this action locks all development on this version. Click Save. The app status changes to RELEASED. The Edit icon in Data Studio and Page Builder will now be disabled for this version. 5 Verify In the App detail, the Status badge shows RELEASED. Open Data Studio → select customer_complaints_<prid> → click the Edit icon. You should see a message that the app is locked for editing.
documents.s: Part C — App Status Lifecycle & Versioning

documents.t: D.1 — Why Branch?​ A Branch creates a parallel ACTIVE copy of your application. Use it when you need to work on next-phase enhancements while the current version is being tested in QA. The branch is fully isolated — changes in the branch don't affect the main RELEASED version until you explicitly merge them. Scenario Use Branch? Bug fix on the current version in QA ❌ No — fix directly in main, create new minor version New feature development while current is in QA ✅ Yes — branch from current ACTIVE version Experimental UI changes for client review ✅ Yes — branch lets you show without committing to main D.2 — Step-by-Step: Creating a Branch​ 1 Go to Account Console → My Apps Locate customer_complaints_<prid>. The app must be in ACTIVE status to create a branch. 2 Click Branch In the app detail view, click the Branch button (visible only when status = ACTIVE). The platform creates a new Branch Flavor automatically. The branch version appears in the My Apps list with a branch indicator. 3 Assign Users to the Branch Click the branch version to open its detail. Go to the Roles & Users tab → click Edit. Assign ALL three test users and your developer account to their respective roles. ⚠ Users are NOT copied automatically from the parent — you must assign them manually in the branch. 4 Develop in the Branch Open Data Studio or Page Builder. In the App dropdown, select the BRANCH version (not the main version). Make your changes. Save and test independently. D.3 — Branch Merge Workflow (Summary)​ When the branch is ready to be merged back into the main release cycle: 1 Export Both ZIPs Account Console → Export section. Download ZIP of the main RELEASED version (Set 1) and the branch version (Set 2). 2 Open App Compare & Merge Account Console → App Compare & Merge. Upload Set 1 (main) as Left and Set 2 (branch) as Right. Click Compare. 3 Review the Differences The tool lists differences per component: entities, pages, queries, VH, menus, etc. For each difference, select which version to keep: Set 1 (main), Set 2 (branch), or a Custom combination. 4 Download Merged ZIP Once all decisions are made, click Download to export the merged ZIP. 5 Create New Version and Import In Account Console, create a new Major or Minor version from the current RELEASED main version. Import the merged ZIP into the new version. Run Update Schema, Full Build, and test before releasing. 📘 Reference / Tip Reference: App Branching & Merging User Guide — App_Branching___Merging-User_Guide.docx PROC-26419 note: 'Account Console' may be renamed 'Workspace Hub' in platform help content. Both names refer to the same tool.

documents.t: E.1 — Validate vs. Publish — What's the Difference?​ Action What It Does When to Use Validate Scans the application for errors WITHOUT building. Safe — nothing changes in the running app. Run first, every time. Fix all errors before triggering Publish. Publish Validates first, then builds the app if no blocking errors exist. Updates the running app. After Validate passes with 0 errors. Use Full Build for first publish or after VH Config changes. E.2 — Common Publish Blockers​ Blocker Cause Fix VH Config not visible in UI after Publish VH Config changes require a Full Build. Always select 'Full Build' for the first publish or after adding/editing VH Configs. TypeScript compilation error Syntax error in entity .ts or controller .ts file. Open VS Code → check terminal for tsc errors → fix, save, re-validate. Update Schema not run Entity properties added but schema not updated in DB. Data Studio → select entity → Update Schema → confirm success toast. Another build IN-QUEUE A previous build is already running. Click 'Proceed' to queue behind the current build. Do NOT cancel it. Missing app_util flavor Validate and Publish menu not visible. Ask trainer — app_util must be assigned to your developer account. E.3 — Step-by-Step: Validate and Publish​ 1 Open Validate and Publish Hamburger menu (☰) → Dev Tools → Validate and Publish. (If this menu item is missing, app_util flavor is not assigned to your account. Ask the trainer.) 2 Enter the Application In the App field, type customer_complaints_<prid> and press Enter. The application version details load. 3 Run Validate First Select Action: Validate. Click Submit. Wait for the validation report to generate. Download the XLSX report if errors are listed. Fix every ERROR before proceeding. Warnings can be reviewed but do not block the build. 4 Fix All Errors For each error in the report: - Missing Update Schema → Data Studio → Update Schema on the entity. - TypeScript error → VS Code → fix tsc error → save → re-validate. - Missing VH Build → select Full Build in the next step. Re-run Validate until the report shows 0 errors. 5 Run Publish Select Action: Publish. Build Type: Full Build (required for first publish and after any VH Config changes). Click Submit. The Publish Log shows the progression: IN-QUEUE → IN-PROCESS → PUBLISHED Do NOT navigate away while the build is running. 6 Verify the Published App Log out completely. Log back in. Open the hamburger menu → confirm 'Complaints' item is visible. Navigate to p_complaints → confirm live data loads. Verify: status badges render, VH dropdowns populate, all tabs in detail section work. 📘 Reference / Tip Publish Logs reference: Publish_Logs_Screen.docx — explains each status stage and error codes. Validate & Publish reference: Publish_or_Validate_Screen-7_0_App_utility__.docx

F.1 — How Transport Works​ Transport is a PULL mechanism: the TARGET system (QA) asks the SOURCE system (DEV) for the latest published version. You perform ALL transport steps while logged into the QA environment, not DEV. Stage What Happens Setup Transport creates entries in QA metadata tables for the application, groups, and flavors. Download Application ZIPs are pulled from DEV and extracted in the QA server's file system. Update Schema Database tables for all entities are created or altered in the QA database. Finalising Application is set to ACTIVE in QA so users can log in and access it. ⚠ Important Transport Pre-requisites — verify ALL before starting 1. The application must be in RELEASED status on the DEV system. 2. Branch flavors CANNOT be transported. Create a new version, merge, then transport. 3. The QA server's config.json must have mm_klo_online_server pointing to the DEV landscape URL. 4. A host file entry for the DEV system must exist on the QA server. 5. The transport_1 app must be assigned to the developer account on the QA system. If any pre-requisite is missing, the transport will fail at Setup or Download stage. Ask the trainer to verify the QA environment config before proceeding. F.2 — Step-by-Step: Transporting to QA​ 1 Log in to the QA System Open the QA environment URL in a browser (trainer provides the URL). Log in with your developer credentials. ⚠ ALL remaining steps are done on QA, not on DEV. 2 Navigate to App Transport Hamburger menu (☰) → Sys Admin → App Transport. The App Transport screen lists all available applications from the connected DEV system. 3 Find Your Application In the list, locate customer_complaints_<prid>. If not visible, toggle the 'Show All' button to see all available apps (not just those with pending updates). 4 Click the App Row Click on customer_complaints_<prid>. A detail panel opens showing available versions from DEV and any already-installed versions in QA. 5 Install As Writable Click the available version update. A dialog appears with two options: As Readable — locked, cannot edit in QA. As Writable — editable, allows continued development in QA. Click 'As Writable' (recommended for training so you can fix issues in QA if needed). 6 Accept Conditions and Proceed A mandatory conditions dialog appears. For each mandatory item (⚠ icon), tick the acceptance checkbox. If prompted about shared flavor movement (on QA/PROD systems), click Proceed. Click Proceed to start the transport. 7 Monitor Transport Stages The screen shows progress through: Setup → Download → Update Schema → Finalising. Wait for each stage to complete. The overall status changes to ACTIVE when done. 8 Assign Users in QA After transport, the app is ACTIVE in QA but has NO users assigned. Go to Account Console → My Apps → customer_complaints_<prid>. Go to Roles & Users tab → assign: emp_<prid> → Employee role mgr_<prid> → Manager role it_<prid> → ResponsibleTeam role Your developer account → Manager role 9 Verify in QA Log out of the QA developer session. Log in as emp_<prid> in QA. Verify: hamburger menu shows 'Complaints', p_complaints loads, all VH dropdowns work. Repeat with mgr_<prid> and it_<prid>. 📘 Reference / Tip Transport User Guide: Transport-_User_Guide.docx The Transport tool supports DEV → QA, QA → PROD, and DEV → DEV movement. Script Master (second tab in Transport screen) shows automated scripts maintained for the system — ask trainer if any scripts need to be run after transport.

All three personas (Employee, Manager, IT Team) have correct access, menu, and data visibility. After this assignment you will have built and shipped a complete enterprise application from scratch. documents.t: Application URLs support version-based access using the following format: https://<domain>/appservice/<landscape>/<flavor>_<version>/<api_id> where <version> follows the format: <major>-<minor>-<patch> When resolving an application version: The specified major and minor versions are honored. The system automatically resolves the request to the latest available patch version within the specified major.minor version. Example​ Available versions: 7-0-1 7-0-5 7-0-20 Request: /appservice/prod/mobile_7-0-1/api123 Resolved Version: 7-0-20 Similarly, if versions 8-1-3, 8-1-10, and 8-2-5 are available: Request: /appservice/prod/mobile_8-1-3/api123 Resolved Version: 8-1-10 This behavior ensures that consumers automatically receive the latest available patch fixes and improvements within the requested major.minor release stream without requiring URL updates.

App overriding is a feature where the child apps inherit the features of the parent app and override their properties. This screen is used to display and highlight the overridden elements and their properties.
Date of Issue: September 2024 Version: 7.0 Prepared by: Nayan Adhikary Target Audience: Application Developers

Maintaining a proper hierarchy between app versions is crucial for accurate dependency management, for this a correct approach to establish a multi-level hierarchy is required, ensuring that dependencies are calculated correctly. To maintain the hierarchy effectively, it always starts from the top-most parent and works your way down to the bottom-most child. Example: Current Versions: A-1 (Top-most Parent) B-1 C-1 D-1 (Bottom-most Child) Correct Hierarchy: A-1 -> B-1 -> C-1 -> D-1 Note: To ensure accurate dependency management; Always maintain hierarchy from the top-most parent to the bottom-most child. This method prevents errors in dependency calculations and keeps the app structure coherent.

This App Lifecycle Events - User Guide provides a structured way for developers to handle various stages of the application's lifecycle. The AppLifeCycleEvent class contains methods that are triggered by the framework to respond to key lifecycle events such as: App start App moves to the foreground App goes into the background App close This allows an efficient and organized management of application behavior in response to above mentioned events. Method Details & Description: Note: All the methods discussed below are Case-sensitive. Please make sure the methods are typed exactly as shown below. No import / export parameters are needed for the below mentioned methods.
Date of Issue: March 2024 Version: 7.0 Target Audience: Application Developer and Admins.
This is a screen that helps make changes in the settings and setting groups that are used in any application.

Note: If the developers want to make any changes to the Settings Definition Screen metadata then they will have to assign core_fw as a dependent app to the fw_settings1_1 app and then build the fw_settings1 flavor and reinitialize it. Only then any changes should be made. Also for save to work, assign is_external for fw_settings1 flavor as 1. To save any changes made on the Settings Definition user needs a shared, writable app.
Flavor: fw_settings1

Go to the menu App Settings. Click on the sub-menu named Settings Definition to open it. The Screen will be loaded initially with all the settings inside their respective Settings Group in a tree in ascending order based on their sequence value. Settings Group will also be in ascending order of their sequence values. Click on the Edit option in the upper right corner of the screen. On the toolbar of the screen, you will find the Create Group, Create Settings, Save, Delete and Cancel buttons. You can create the settings group by clicking the +Group button on the top right of the screen. It will ask the developer to provide the Settings Group ID in an input dialog. Click on the Create button in the input dialog. After creating a new Settings Group, users can see it updated in the Table Tree below. Users need to fill in the Sequence number, Title and Icon of that settings group and then click on the Save button to save the newly created settings group. All the settings groups will now be shown in ascending order of their sequence value. The developer then needs to create Settings inside the newly created settings group. To do that the user needs to select that settings group on the tree and then click on +Setting Button. It will ask for the Settings ID under Create Setting and the developer needs to provide the ID and click on the Create button. A new setting will be created inside the selected settings group. The developer needs to fill in the Title, Description, Sequence Number, Icon, Data Type, UI type, Vh ID, Default value, visible and modifiable_in and then click on Save to save all the changes. After successful save, all the settings in their respective groups will be in ascending order of their sequence value. Components Descriptions Title It's the name you want to put to identify the setting control. Description A short description of the setting element. Sequence Number This will put the setting elements according to the order of its sequence. Icon This implies an individual settings icon. Data Type It's the type of the setting, whether it's a number, an integer or a string etc. UI Type It is the type of Control that you want to render in the UI for those Settings such as Input, Slider, value Help, etc. Vh ID It is the value help ID created from bol editor on application flavor and it will be shown to the user as value help items in case the user has chosen UI type as VH. Default Value It's a pre-value that has been set for some particular setting. This is changeable according to your requirements. visible This implies who will be able to see the particular setting item. modifiable in This puts down conditions on who can see the setting items and so on. To update any details click on the edit button in the toolbar and after updating the details click on save to commit the changes. If you have updated any details and do not want it to commit then you can click on the reset button in the toolbar to set the details to the original state.

documents.t: Add a value to an input or textarea element found by the given selector.Send a sequence of keystrokes to an element after the input has been cleared before. documents.t: The "replaceMap" action is utilized for incorporating additional variables that can be utilized across all files during runtime. This method proves beneficial for transmitting parameters within our functions, given that direct argument passing isn't feasible in array format. By employing this workaround, we simulate the behavior of passing arguments as done conventionally in regular functions. Note :- For the "replaceMap" action, an additional key-value pair, "data", must be included in the object. The "data" attribute is designed to store an array of objects, each representing a variable and its value that you wish to declare or store within the replaceMap. Upon repeated use of the same variables within replaceMap, it will overwrite the older values with the newly assigned ones. In the provided example, you'll notice the absence of "controlID" or "domElementId". This is because no actions were performed on any specific element; hence, the user needs to craft this function manually instead of generating it through a test recorder. Same will happen with many actions that are not performed on any elements.

If the element is disabled or not visible and you still want to receive the text content use getHTML as a workaround. This action uses the “.getText()” API of WDIO. For more reference click here. Note: For the "getText" action, an additional key-value pair, "storeAt", must be included in the object.The "storeAt" parameter will contain the name of the variable($variable_name$), where you intend to save the retrieved value from the chosen control element. getText action is only used in the places where there is only text field like sap.m.text,sap.m.label etc it will not work on input fields like klarion’s kloInput or sap.m.input.

documents.t: The "ifPresent" action serves as a mechanism for verifying certain operations executed during automation. Specifically, it checks if a selected control element is indeed displayed on the screen. By utilizing its domElementId, it searches for the presence of the DOM element on the screen. Note: For the "ifPresent" action, an extra key-value pair named "type" needs to be added to the object. The "type" parameter specifies the kind of control that the action targets. This "type" should match the "controlType" found within the controlID.

documents.t: The "ifNotPresent" action functions as a counterpart to "ifPresent," serving to verify specific actions carried out during automation but in reverse. It specifically verifies whether a chosen control element is absent from the screen. Utilizing its domElementId, it searches to confirm the absence of the DOM element on the screen.

documents.t: Dispatch a series of keystrokes to the currently focused ("active") element. Activating an input element can be achieved simply by clicking on it.
